question: How do I check the Windows version I'm using?
answer: Press the Windows key + R, type 'winver', and press Enter. A dialog box will appear showing your Windows version and build number. Alternatively, go to Settings > System > About to see more detailed information.

question: How do I update Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update, then click 'Check for updates'. Windows will download and install any available updates. It's recommended to restart your PC after updates are installed to apply them fully.

question: How do I factory reset Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Recovery. Under 'Reset this PC', click 'Get started' and choose whether to keep your files or remove everything. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the reset.

question: How do I uninstall a program in Windows?
answer: Open Settings > Apps > Apps & Features, find the program in the list, click on it, and select 'Uninstall'. Alternatively, right-click the Start button and choose 'Apps and Features'. Some programs may require you to run their own uninstaller.

question: How do I take a screenshot in Windows?
answer: Press the Print Screen (PrtScn) key to copy the entire screen to clipboard, then paste it into an image editor. Press Windows + Print Screen to save a screenshot directly to the Screenshots folder in Pictures. Press Windows + Shift + S to open Snip & Sketch for a custom selection.

question: How do I enable dark mode in Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > Personalization > Colors. Under 'Choose your color', select 'Dark'. This changes Windows, apps, and the taskbar to dark mode. Some apps may have their own separate dark mode settings.

question: How do I manage startup programs in Windows?
answer: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager, then click the 'Startup' tab. Here you can see all programs that launch at startup and disable any you don't need. Disabling unnecessary startup programs can significantly improve boot time.

question: How do I format a USB drive in Windows?
answer: Right-click the USB drive in File Explorer and select 'Format'. Choose the file system (NTFS for large files, FAT32 for compatibility), give it a name, and click 'Start'. Be aware that formatting erases all data on the drive.

question: How do I map a network drive in Windows?
answer: Open File Explorer, click 'This PC', then select 'Map network drive' from the Computer tab. Choose a drive letter, enter the folder path (e.g., \\server\share), and check 'Reconnect at sign-in' if you want it to persist. Click Finish and enter credentials if prompted.

question: How do I enable Remote Desktop on Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > System > Remote Desktop and toggle 'Enable Remote Desktop' to On. Note that Remote Desktop is only available on Windows 10 Pro, Enterprise, or Education editions. You'll need the PC's IP address or name to connect remotely.

question: How do I change the default browser in Windows?
answer: Go to Settings > Apps > Default Apps. Scroll down to 'Web browser' and click on the current browser shown. A list of installed browsers will appear — select your preferred one. You can also set defaults per file type or protocol from the same page.

question: What is the difference between 32-bit and 64-bit Windows?
answer: 64-bit Windows can use more than 4 GB of RAM and run both 32-bit and 64-bit applications, while 32-bit Windows is limited to about 4 GB of RAM. Most modern computers and software are 64-bit. You can check your system type in Settings > System > About.

question: How do I access the Windows Registry?
answer: Press Windows + R, type 'regedit', and press Enter. The Registry Editor will open, giving access to system configuration settings. Be very careful when editing the registry — incorrect changes can cause system instability or prevent Windows from booting.

question: How do I check disk health in Windows?
answer: Open Command Prompt as administrator and type 'wmic diskdrive get status'. You can also use 'chkdsk C: /f /r' to scan and repair disk errors. For a more detailed view, third-party tools like CrystalDiskInfo show S.M.A.R.T. data and overall drive health.

question: How do I change the screen resolution in Windows?
answer: Right-click on the desktop and select 'Display settings'. Scroll to 'Display resolution' and choose your preferred resolution from the dropdown. The recommended resolution for your monitor is usually labeled — click 'Keep changes' to confirm.

question: How do I create a local user account in Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > Accounts > Family & other users. Click 'Add someone else to this PC', then select 'I don't have this person's sign-in information', followed by 'Add a user without a Microsoft account'. Enter a username and password to complete setup.

question: How do I speed up a slow Windows computer?
answer: Disable unnecessary startup programs via Task Manager > Startup tab. Run Disk Cleanup to remove temporary files, and check for malware using Windows Defender. Upgrading to an SSD or adding more RAM will have the most significant performance impact.

question: How do I recover deleted files in Windows?
answer: Check the Recycle Bin first — if the file is there, right-click and select 'Restore'. If it's been emptied, try the 'Previous Versions' feature by right-clicking the folder. Third-party tools like Recuva can often recover files even after the Recycle Bin has been emptied.

question: What is Windows Defender and how do I use it?
answer: Windows Defender is Microsoft's built-in antivirus and antimalware tool. Access it via Settings > Update & Security > Windows Security. It runs automatically in the background but you can run manual scans, view threat history, and manage firewall settings from the dashboard.

question: How do I change the date and time in Windows?
answer: Right-click the clock in the taskbar and select 'Adjust date/time'. You can toggle 'Set time automatically' on or off, and manually set the date and time if needed. Make sure the correct time zone is selected to keep your clock accurate.

question: How do I install Linux alongside Windows (dual boot)?
answer: Create a bootable USB with your Linux distribution using a tool like Rufus. Shrink your Windows partition in Disk Management to make space, then boot from the USB and run the Linux installer. When prompted, choose 'Install alongside Windows' and the installer will handle the bootloader setup.

question: How do I update software on Ubuntu Linux?
answer: Open a terminal and run 'sudo apt update' to refresh the package list, then 'sudo apt upgrade' to install available updates. You can also use the Software Updater graphical tool. Running 'sudo apt full-upgrade' handles dependency changes as well.

question: How do I check disk usage in Linux?
answer: Run 'df -h' in the terminal to see disk space usage for all mounted filesystems in a human-readable format. To see the size of specific directories, use 'du -sh /path/to/directory'. The 'ncdu' tool provides an interactive disk usage viewer.

question: How do I create a new user in Linux?
answer: Use the command 'sudo adduser username' in the terminal and follow the prompts to set a password and user details. To give the user sudo (administrator) privileges, run 'sudo usermod -aG sudo username'. Verify the user was created with 'cat /etc/passwd'.

question: How do I check running processes in Linux?
answer: Run 'ps aux' to see all running processes, or use 'top' for a real-time interactive view. The 'htop' command (install with sudo apt install htop) provides a more user-friendly interface with color coding and easy process management.

question: How do I change file permissions in Linux?
answer: Use the 'chmod' command followed by a permission code and filename, e.g., 'chmod 755 script.sh'. The digits represent owner, group, and others permissions (4=read, 2=write, 1=execute). You can also use symbolic notation like 'chmod u+x file' to add execute permission for the owner.

question: How do I install software on Linux using the terminal?
answer: For Debian/Ubuntu-based systems, use 'sudo apt install packagename'. For Red Hat/Fedora systems, use 'sudo dnf install packagename'. Always run 'sudo apt update' first to refresh the package index before installing new software.

question: How do I view hidden files in Linux?
answer: In the terminal, use 'ls -a' to list all files including hidden ones (those starting with a dot). In most graphical file managers, press Ctrl + H to toggle the display of hidden files. Hidden configuration files are typically found in your home directory.

question: How do I schedule tasks in Linux using cron?
answer: Edit the cron table with 'crontab -e' and add a line with the schedule and command. The format is: minute hour day month weekday command. For example, '0 2 * * * /path/to/script.sh' runs a script at 2 AM every day. Use 'crontab -l' to list existing cron jobs.

question: How do I check system logs in Linux?
answer: Use 'journalctl' to view systemd logs, or check '/var/log/' directory for log files. 'journalctl -u servicename' shows logs for a specific service, and 'journalctl -f' follows new log entries in real time. For older syslog-based systems, check '/var/log/syslog'.

question: How do I find a file in Linux using the terminal?
answer: Use the 'find' command: 'find /path -name filename'. For example, 'find / -name myfile.txt' searches the entire filesystem. The 'locate' command is faster but requires an up-to-date database — run 'sudo updatedb' first. Use 'grep -r text /path' to search file contents.

question: How do I compress and extract files in Linux?
answer: To create a tar.gz archive: 'tar -czvf archive.tar.gz foldername'. To extract: 'tar -xzvf archive.tar.gz'. For zip files, use 'zip -r archive.zip folder' and 'unzip archive.zip'. The '-v' flag shows verbose output during the operation.

question: How do I check my macOS version?
answer: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner and select 'About This Mac'. The macOS version and build number are displayed prominently. You can also run 'sw_vers' in Terminal for version details from the command line.

question: How do I update macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences (or System Settings on macOS Ventura and later) and click 'Software Update'. macOS will check for and display available updates. It's recommended to back up your Mac with Time Machine before a major OS update.

question: How do I take a screenshot on a Mac?
answer: Press Command + Shift + 3 to capture the entire screen. Press Command + Shift + 4 to draw a selection area. Press Command + Shift + 5 to open the screenshot toolbar with more options including screen recording. Screenshots are saved to the Desktop by default.

question: How do I force quit an application on Mac?
answer: Press Command + Option + Esc to open the Force Quit Applications window, select the unresponsive app, and click 'Force Quit'. You can also right-click (or Ctrl-click) the app's icon in the Dock and hold Option to change 'Quit' to 'Force Quit'.

question: How do I clear cache on macOS?
answer: In the Finder, press Command + Shift + G and go to ~/Library/Caches. Delete the contents of this folder to clear application caches. For browser caches, use the browser's own settings. Tools like CleanMyMac or OnyX can automate this process more safely.

question: How do I install apps on a Mac?
answer: Download apps from the Mac App Store by clicking 'Get' or 'Buy'. For apps outside the App Store, download the .dmg file, open it, and drag the app to the Applications folder. You may need to allow apps from identified developers in System Preferences > Security & Privacy.

question: How do I enable FileVault disk encryption on Mac?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Security & Privacy > FileVault and click 'Turn On FileVault'. You'll be prompted to choose a recovery method — either through your iCloud account or a recovery key. Encryption happens in the background and may take several hours to complete.

question: How do I use Time Machine for backups on Mac?
answer: Connect an external drive, go to System Preferences > Time Machine, and click 'Select Backup Disk'. Choose your external drive and Time Machine will automatically back up your Mac hourly, daily, and weekly. Keep the backup drive connected regularly for continuous protection.

question: How do I reset the NVRAM on a Mac?
answer: Shut down your Mac and turn it on while holding Command + Option + P + R for about 20 seconds until you hear the startup sound twice (on older Macs) or see the Apple logo appear and disappear twice. NVRAM stores settings like sound volume, display resolution, and startup disk selection.

question: What is Homebrew and how do I install it on macOS?
answer: Homebrew is a package manager for macOS that makes it easy to install developer tools and command-line software. Install it by running the command from brew.sh in Terminal: /bin/bash -c '$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)'. Then use 'brew install packagename' to install software.

question: How do I set up SSH key authentication?
answer: Generate a key pair with 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519' and follow the prompts. Copy the public key to the server with 'ssh-copy-id user@server'. SSH will then use your private key instead of a password. Store your private key securely and never share it.

question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
answer: A process is an independent program running in its own memory space, while a thread is a unit of execution within a process that shares the process's memory. Multiple threads in one process can run concurrently, making multithreaded applications faster. Processes are isolated from each other for security and stability.

question: How do I set environment variables in Windows?
answer: Right-click 'This PC', select Properties, then 'Advanced system settings' > 'Environment Variables'. You can add user or system-wide variables there. Alternatively, set a temporary variable in Command Prompt with 'set VARNAME=value', or permanently via PowerShell with '[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable'.

question: How do I set environment variables in Linux or macOS?
answer: Add 'export VARNAME=value' to your shell profile file (~/.bashrc for Bash, ~/.zshrc for Zsh) to make it permanent. Run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply changes immediately. Use 'echo $VARNAME' to verify the variable is set, or 'printenv' to list all environment variables.

question: What is a virtual machine and how do I create one?
answer: A virtual machine (VM) is a software emulation of a computer that runs inside your actual computer. Use tools like VirtualBox or VMware to create one — download the software, create a new VM, allocate CPU and RAM, attach an OS ISO file, and install the OS as you would on a real machine.

question: How do I transfer files between Windows and Linux?
answer: Use SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) from the command line: 'scp file user@linuxhost:/path'. On Windows, WinSCP or FileZilla provide graphical interfaces for SFTP transfers. Samba shares can also be set up to make Linux folders accessible as Windows network drives.

question: What is WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) and how do I enable it?
answer: WSL lets you run a Linux environment directly on Windows without a VM. Enable it by running 'wsl --install' in PowerShell as administrator, which installs WSL2 and Ubuntu by default. After a restart, open the Ubuntu app to set up your Linux username and password.

question: How do I partition a hard drive in Windows?
answer: Right-click the Start button and open 'Disk Management'. Right-click an existing partition and select 'Shrink Volume' to free up space, then right-click the unallocated space and choose 'New Simple Volume'. Follow the wizard to assign a drive letter and format the partition.

question: How do I check CPU and RAM usage in Windows?
answer: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager and click the 'Performance' tab. This shows real-time graphs for CPU, memory, disk, and network usage. For more detailed monitoring, use Resource Monitor (search in Start menu) or the Performance Monitor tool.

question: What is the difference between HDD and SSD?
answer: An HDD (Hard Disk Drive) uses spinning magnetic platters to store data and is slower but cheaper per gigabyte. An SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory, has no moving parts, and is significantly faster, more durable, and quieter. For most users, an SSD as the primary drive greatly improves system responsiveness.

question: How do I install RAM in a desktop PC?
answer: Power off and unplug the PC, then open the case. Locate the RAM slots on the motherboard, press down the retention clips, and align the RAM stick with the slot notch. Press firmly until the clips click into place. Ensure you install RAM in matched pairs in the correct slots as shown in the motherboard manual.

question: How do I check if my RAM is faulty?
answer: Run the Windows Memory Diagnostic tool by searching for it in the Start menu — it will test your RAM on next restart. Alternatively, use MemTest86, a bootable tool that performs thorough memory testing. Common symptoms of faulty RAM include random crashes, BSODs, and system instability.

question: How do I clean my computer keyboard?
answer: Turn the keyboard upside down and shake gently to dislodge debris. Use compressed air to blow out dust between the keys. For sticky keys, use a cotton swab lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol. For a deep clean, keycaps can be removed on mechanical keyboards and soaked in warm soapy water.

question: What causes a computer to overheat and how do I fix it?
answer: Overheating is usually caused by dust buildup blocking airflow, a failing or inadequate cooling fan, or dried thermal paste on the CPU. Clean the inside of the PC with compressed air, ensure all case fans are working, and consider reapplying thermal paste to the CPU if the system is several years old.

question: How do I replace a laptop battery?
answer: Check your laptop model and order a compatible replacement battery. For most modern laptops, power off the device, remove the bottom panel screws, disconnect the old battery connector from the motherboard, and swap in the new battery. Some laptops have glued batteries that require more care and specialized tools.

question: How do I connect multiple monitors to a PC?
answer: Check what video outputs your graphics card or motherboard has (HDMI, DisplayPort, DVI, VGA). Connect each monitor using the appropriate cable. Right-click the desktop in Windows, select 'Display settings', and configure the layout, resolution, and orientation of each screen.

question: What is thermal paste and when should I replace it?
answer: Thermal paste fills microscopic gaps between the CPU and its heatsink to improve heat transfer. It should be replaced every 3–5 years or if temperatures are abnormally high. To replace it, clean off the old paste with isopropyl alcohol, apply a small pea-sized amount of new paste to the center of the CPU, then reseat the cooler.

question: How do I diagnose a monitor with no display?
answer: Check that the monitor is powered on and the cable is firmly connected to both the monitor and the PC. Try a different cable or port. Connect the monitor to another computer to determine if the issue is with the monitor or the PC. If the PC runs but shows no display, the GPU or display output port may be faulty.

question: How do I install a new graphics card?
answer: Power off and unplug the PC. Remove the old GPU by unscrewing it from the case bracket and releasing the PCIe slot clip. Insert the new GPU firmly into the PCIe x16 slot until it clicks. Screw it to the bracket, connect the PCIe power cables, then install the drivers after booting.

question: What is the difference between PCIe Gen 3 and Gen 4?
answer: PCIe Gen 4 doubles the bandwidth per lane compared to Gen 3, going from 1 GB/s to 2 GB/s per lane. This benefits high-speed NVMe SSDs and high-end GPUs. Most current consumer components support Gen 4, and Gen 5 is emerging. Backward compatibility means Gen 4 devices work in Gen 3 slots at reduced speed.

question: How do I install an M.2 SSD?
answer: Locate the M.2 slot on your motherboard (check the manual). Remove the retaining screw, slide the M.2 SSD in at a slight angle into the slot, press it down flat, and secure it with the screw. Ensure the M.2 drive is compatible with the slot (NVMe vs SATA, correct form factor like 2280).

question: How do I fix a USB device not recognized error?
answer: Try a different USB port or cable. Open Device Manager and look for any devices with a yellow warning icon. Right-click and choose 'Update driver' or 'Uninstall device' then reconnect it. Disabling USB Selective Suspend in Power Options can also resolve intermittent recognition issues.

question: How do I check my power supply unit (PSU) wattage?
answer: Open your PC case and find the label on the side of the PSU, which lists its maximum wattage. You can also use a PSU calculator (available online) to determine how much wattage your components require. Running a PSU near its maximum capacity shortens its lifespan.

question: What is the difference between a mechanical and membrane keyboard?
answer: Mechanical keyboards use individual switches under each key that provide tactile feedback, distinct click sounds (on clicky switches), and longer lifespan. Membrane keyboards use a pressure pad beneath the keys, are quieter and cheaper, but offer less tactile feedback. Mechanical keyboards are preferred by typists and gamers.

question: How do I calibrate my monitor?
answer: Windows has a built-in calibration tool under Display settings > Advanced display settings > Color calibration. For professional results, use a hardware colorimeter like the X-Rite i1Display. Adjust brightness, contrast, gamma, and color temperature to match your work environment and use case.

question: What is the difference between 1080p, 1440p, and 4K resolution?
answer: 1080p (Full HD) is 1920x1080 pixels, 1440p (2K/QHD) is 2560x1440, and 4K (UHD) is 3840x2160. Higher resolution means sharper images but requires more GPU power to drive at high frame rates. For gaming, 1440p at high refresh rates is currently a popular balance of clarity and performance.

question: How do I fix a printer that won't print?
answer: Check that the printer is powered on, connected, and has paper and ink/toner. Open the printer queue (Settings > Devices > Printers) and clear any stuck jobs. Try printing a test page from the printer's own settings. Reinstalling the printer driver often resolves persistent issues.

question: How do I connect a Bluetooth device to my computer?
answer: Ensure Bluetooth is enabled on your PC (Settings > Devices > Bluetooth). Put the Bluetooth device in pairing mode (usually by holding a button). Your PC will discover the device — click on it and select 'Pair'. Follow any PIN prompts to complete the pairing.

question: What is RAID and how does it work?
answer: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) combines multiple drives for redundancy or performance. RAID 0 stripes data across drives for speed but offers no redundancy. RAID 1 mirrors data for redundancy. RAID 5 and RAID 6 provide a balance of performance and fault tolerance. RAID is not a substitute for backups.

question: How do I extend my laptop screen to an external monitor?
answer: Connect the monitor to your laptop via HDMI, DisplayPort, or USB-C. Press Windows + P on Windows to choose display mode: Duplicate, Extend, or Second screen only. On Mac, go to System Preferences > Displays and arrange the screens. Use Extend mode to gain additional desktop workspace.

question: What causes a CPU to throttle and how do I prevent it?
answer: CPU throttling (thermal throttling) occurs when the processor gets too hot and reduces its clock speed to cool down. It's typically caused by poor cooling, dust buildup, or dried thermal paste. Cleaning the cooler, reapplying thermal paste, and ensuring good case airflow help prevent throttling.

question: How do I replace a desktop PC's CPU cooler?
answer: Power off and unplug the PC. Remove the existing cooler by detaching its retention mechanism (push pins or screws). Clean off the old thermal paste with isopropyl alcohol. Apply fresh thermal paste, mount the new cooler according to its instructions, and connect the fan header to the motherboard.

question: How do I identify what hardware is in my PC?
answer: Use CPU-Z or HWiNFO64 for detailed hardware information including CPU, RAM, motherboard, and GPU specs. On Windows, Device Manager and System Information (msinfo32) also provide component lists. On Linux, use 'lshw -short' or 'inxi -Fx' for a comprehensive hardware summary.

question: What is the purpose of a PC case fan?
answer: Case fans improve airflow through the computer chassis, drawing cool air in and expelling hot air out. Proper airflow keeps components like the CPU, GPU, and storage drives at safe temperatures. Typically, front/bottom fans intake cool air while rear/top fans exhaust hot air.

question: How do I add more storage to my laptop?
answer: Many laptops allow you to replace or add an M.2 SSD or 2.5-inch SATA drive — check your model's service manual. If internal expansion isn't possible, a USB 3.x external SSD offers fast, portable storage. For very large storage needs, a USB 3.0 external hard drive is cost-effective.

question: What is ECC RAM and who needs it?
answer: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM detects and corrects single-bit memory errors on the fly, preventing data corruption. It's used in servers, workstations, and systems where data integrity is critical, such as databases and scientific computing. ECC RAM requires compatible motherboards and processors, and it's generally more expensive than standard RAM.

question: How do I fix a computer that won't boot after new hardware installation?
answer: Reseat all newly installed components — RAM, GPU, and drives — to ensure they're fully connected. Reset the BIOS by removing the CMOS battery for 30 seconds or using the clear CMOS jumper. Check that all power connectors are firmly attached. If the system still won't boot, try removing new hardware one piece at a time to isolate the faulty component.

question: What is the difference between a wired and wireless mouse?
answer: A wired mouse connects via USB and offers zero latency and no need for charging. A wireless mouse uses Bluetooth or a USB dongle, providing freedom of movement at the cost of occasional latency and battery maintenance. Modern wireless gaming mice have become competitive with wired ones in terms of response time.

question: How do I troubleshoot a monitor flickering issue?
answer: Check and reseat the video cable at both ends. Try a different cable or port type (e.g., swap HDMI for DisplayPort). Update your GPU drivers and check the monitor's refresh rate in Display settings. A flickering monitor can also indicate a failing panel backlight, which may require professional repair or replacement.

question: What is the difference between a router and a modem?
answer: A modem connects your home network to your internet service provider (ISP) by modulating/demodulating the signal from the cable or phone line. A router connects multiple devices within your home and routes traffic between them and the internet. Many ISPs provide a combined modem-router unit called a gateway.

question: How do I find my IP address?
answer: On Windows, open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig' — your IP address is listed under IPv4 Address. On macOS/Linux, use 'ifconfig' or 'ip addr' in Terminal. Your public IP address (visible to the internet) can be found by visiting a site like whatismyip.com.

question: What is the difference between 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi?
answer: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi has better range and penetrates walls more effectively but is slower and more prone to interference from other devices. 5 GHz Wi-Fi offers faster speeds and less interference but has a shorter range. Use 5 GHz for devices close to the router requiring high bandwidth, and 2.4 GHz for devices farther away.

question: How do I change my Wi-Fi password?
answer: Log into your router's admin interface by entering its IP address (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1) in a browser. Find the Wireless or Wi-Fi settings section and update the password. Save the settings and reconnect all your devices with the new password.

question: How do I set up a VPN on Windows?
answer: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > VPN and click 'Add a VPN connection'. Enter the VPN provider's server address, connection name, and your credentials. Alternatively, install your VPN provider's app (e.g., NordVPN, ExpressVPN) for a simpler setup with automatic server selection.

question: What is DNS and how does it work?
answer: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names (like google.com) into IP addresses that computers use to communicate. When you type a URL, your device queries a DNS server to resolve it. You can change your DNS server in network settings — popular alternatives include Google DNS (8.8.8.8) and Cloudflare (1.1.1.1).

question: How do I extend my Wi-Fi coverage?
answer: You can use a Wi-Fi range extender/repeater that amplifies the existing signal. A mesh network system (like Google Nest or Eero) is a more seamless solution using multiple nodes. For the best performance, consider powerline adapters that use your home's electrical wiring to extend a wired connection.

question: What is a firewall and how does it protect my network?
answer: A firewall monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks connections that don't meet defined security rules. Windows includes a built-in firewall (Windows Defender Firewall). Home routers also have built-in NAT firewalls. Enterprise environments use dedicated hardware firewalls for more granular control.

question: How do I check if my internet connection is working?
answer: Open a web browser and try loading a website. If it fails, ping a public server: open Command Prompt and type 'ping 8.8.8.8'. If the ping works but websites don't load, it may be a DNS issue. If ping fails too, the connection itself is down — restart your modem and router.

question: What is NAT and why is it used?
answer: NAT (Network Address Translation) allows multiple devices on a local network to share a single public IP address. The router translates private IP addresses (e.g., 192.168.x.x) to the public IP when communicating with the internet. NAT provides a basic layer of security by hiding internal devices from direct external access.

question: How do I set a static IP address for a device on my network?
answer: The best method is to assign a DHCP reservation in your router's settings, linking the device's MAC address to a fixed IP. Alternatively, set a static IP directly on the device in its network adapter settings, ensuring you choose an address outside the router's DHCP range. Static IPs are useful for servers and printers.

question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
answer: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) ensures reliable, ordered delivery of data with error checking, making it ideal for web browsing, email, and file transfers. UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is faster but doesn't guarantee delivery, making it suitable for video streaming, VoIP, and online gaming where speed matters more than perfection.

question: How do I port forward on my router?
answer: Log into your router's admin interface, find the 'Port Forwarding' or 'Virtual Server' section, and add a new rule specifying the external port, internal IP address, and internal port. This directs incoming traffic on the specified port to a device inside your network, commonly used for gaming servers or remote access.

question: What is a MAC address and how is it different from an IP address?
answer: A MAC address is a unique hardware identifier assigned to a network interface card by the manufacturer, used for communication within a local network. An IP address is a logical address assigned by the network for routing traffic across the internet. IP addresses can change; MAC addresses are generally fixed.

question: How do I run a network speed test?
answer: Visit speedtest.net or fast.com in your browser to measure your current download and upload speeds. For command-line testing, use 'speedtest-cli' on Linux/macOS. For accurate results, connect via ethernet cable and close other applications. Compare results to your ISP's advertised speeds.

question: What is DHCP and how does it work?
answer: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, gateways, and DNS servers to devices joining a network. Your router typically acts as a DHCP server. Without DHCP, you'd need to manually configure IP settings on every device. DHCP leases are temporary and renewed periodically.

question: How do I troubleshoot a slow internet connection?
answer: First, run a speed test to see your actual speeds. Restart your modem and router. Check if other devices are also slow — if so, the issue is likely with the router or ISP. Move closer to the router or connect via ethernet. Check for background downloads, and consider upgrading your plan if speeds are consistently below what you pay for.

question: What is a subnet mask and why does it matter?
answer: A subnet mask defines which part of an IP address identifies the network and which part identifies the host. For example, a mask of 255.255.255.0 means the first three octets are the network. Subnetting allows network administrators to divide large networks into smaller, more manageable segments.

question: How do I check which devices are connected to my Wi-Fi?
answer: Log into your router's admin page and look for a 'Connected Devices' or 'DHCP Clients' section, which lists all devices by name or MAC address. You can also use network scanning tools like 'nmap' or apps like Fing to discover devices on your network.

question: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
answer: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) transmits data in plain text, while HTTPS (HTTP Secure) encrypts data using TLS/SSL. HTTPS protects sensitive data like passwords and credit card numbers from interception. Browsers show a padlock icon for HTTPS sites. Websites without HTTPS are flagged as 'Not secure' in modern browsers.

question: How do I set up a home NAS (Network Attached Storage)?
answer: Purchase a NAS device (e.g., Synology, QNAP) or repurpose an old PC with NAS software like TrueNAS. Install hard drives, connect the NAS to your router, and access it via the web interface to configure storage pools and shared folders. Install the vendor's app to access files from all your devices.

question: What is a VLAN and when would I use one?
answer: A VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) logically separates devices on the same physical network into different network segments. Common uses include isolating IoT devices from your main network, separating guest Wi-Fi, and segmenting a company's departments. VLANs require a managed switch and router that supports VLAN tagging.

question: How does Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) differ from Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac)?
answer: Wi-Fi 6 offers higher theoretical maximum speeds, better performance in congested environments (using OFDMA and BSS Coloring), and improved battery efficiency for client devices through Target Wake Time. While Wi-Fi 5 is still sufficient for most home users, Wi-Fi 6 shines in environments with many simultaneously connected devices.

question: What is a ping and how do I interpret the results?
answer: Ping sends ICMP echo request packets to a host and measures the round-trip time in milliseconds (ms). A lower ping indicates a faster connection. 'Request timed out' means the host isn't responding or is blocking ICMP. High or inconsistent (jitter) ping values affect real-time applications like gaming and video calls.

question: How do I configure a static route on a network?
answer: On Windows, use 'route add [destination] mask [subnet] [gateway]' in an elevated Command Prompt. On Linux, use 'ip route add [destination]/[prefix] via [gateway]'. To make it persistent across reboots on Linux, add the route to '/etc/network/interfaces' or a Netplan config depending on your distribution.

question: What is the difference between a hub, switch, and router?
answer: A hub broadcasts data to all devices on the network, creating unnecessary traffic. A switch is smarter — it learns device MAC addresses and sends data only to the intended recipient. A router connects different networks together (e.g., your LAN to the internet) and makes decisions based on IP addresses.

question: How do I block a device from accessing my Wi-Fi?
answer: Log into your router admin panel and find MAC filtering or access control settings. Add the device's MAC address to the block list. You can also change your Wi-Fi password and reconnect only trusted devices. Some routers allow scheduling internet access per device.

question: What is QoS (Quality of Service) and how do I configure it?
answer: QoS lets your router prioritize certain types of traffic or specific devices. For example, you can prioritize video conferencing or gaming traffic over file downloads. Access QoS settings through your router's admin interface and assign priority levels to devices or application ports.

question: How do I configure IPv6 on my network?
answer: IPv6 is usually enabled by default on modern routers and operating systems. Check your router's WAN settings for IPv6 configuration — options include SLAAC, DHCPv6, or manual configuration depending on your ISP. You can verify IPv6 connectivity by visiting test-ipv6.com.

question: What tools can I use for network monitoring?
answer: Popular tools include Wireshark for packet capture and analysis, PRTG Network Monitor or Zabbix for infrastructure monitoring, and Nagios for alerts and uptime monitoring. For home networks, the Fing app gives quick visibility into connected devices and their status.

question: What is two-factor authentication (2FA) and how do I enable it?
answer: Two-factor authentication adds a second verification step beyond your password, such as a code from an app or SMS. Enable it in your account's security settings — most major services like Google, Facebook, and banking apps support it. Use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy for better security than SMS.

question: How do I create a strong password?
answer: A strong password is at least 12 characters long and combines uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. Avoid dictionary words, names, or predictable patterns. Use a passphrase (a string of random words) for memorability. Better yet, use a password manager to generate and store truly random passwords.

question: What is a password manager and which one should I use?
answer: A password manager securely stores all your passwords in an encrypted vault, accessible with one master password. Popular options include Bitwarden (free and open-source), 1Password, Dashlane, and LastPass. They can generate strong passwords and autofill them, eliminating the need to remember multiple credentials.

question: How do I recognize a phishing email?
answer: Look for mismatched or misspelled sender email addresses, urgent language pressuring immediate action, suspicious links (hover to preview the URL), unexpected attachments, and generic greetings like 'Dear Customer'. Legitimate companies will never ask for your password via email. When in doubt, contact the company directly through their official website.

question: What is ransomware and how can I protect myself?
answer: Ransomware is malware that encrypts your files and demands payment for the decryption key. Protect yourself by keeping software updated, not clicking suspicious links, using reputable antivirus software, and maintaining regular offline backups. Never pay the ransom, as it doesn't guarantee file recovery.

question: How do I check if my email or password has been compromised?
answer: Visit haveibeenpwned.com and enter your email address — it checks against a database of known data breaches. Enable breach alerts so you're notified if your data appears in future leaks. If a breach is found, immediately change the password for that service and anywhere else you used the same password.

question: What is a VPN and does it make me anonymous online?
answer: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) encrypts your internet traffic and routes it through a server in another location, hiding your real IP address from websites. However, it doesn't make you completely anonymous — your VPN provider can see your traffic, and cookies/browser fingerprinting can still track you. It's most useful on public Wi-Fi.

question: How do I secure my home Wi-Fi network?
answer: Change the default router admin username and password. Set Wi-Fi encryption to WPA3 or WPA2. Use a strong, unique Wi-Fi password. Disable WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) as it has known vulnerabilities. Keep your router firmware updated. Consider creating a separate guest network for visitors and IoT devices.

question: What is the principle of least privilege?
answer: The principle of least privilege means giving users, processes, and systems only the minimum permissions they need to do their job. This limits the damage if an account is compromised. In practice, it means using standard user accounts for daily tasks, not admin accounts, and restricting employee access to only the systems they need.

question: How do I protect my computer from viruses?
answer: Install and keep updated a reputable antivirus program. Keep your OS and apps updated to patch security vulnerabilities. Avoid downloading software from untrusted sources. Don't open unexpected email attachments. Use a firewall. Regularly back up your data so you can recover from an infection without paying ransom.

question: What is social engineering in cybersecurity?
answer: Social engineering manipulates people into revealing confidential information or performing actions that compromise security — rather than attacking systems directly. Examples include phishing emails, pretexting (creating false scenarios), and vishing (voice phishing). Human awareness and training are the primary defenses.

question: What is a zero-day vulnerability?
answer: A zero-day vulnerability is a software flaw that is unknown to the software vendor and for which no patch exists yet. Attackers who discover these can exploit them before a fix is available. Zero-days are highly valuable and often used in targeted attacks. Keeping software updated minimizes your exposure when patches are eventually released.

question: What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
answer: Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt data, making it fast but requiring secure key exchange. Asymmetric encryption uses a public/private key pair — the public key encrypts data, and only the matching private key can decrypt it. HTTPS uses asymmetric encryption to establish a secure session, then symmetric encryption for speed.

question: How do I enable Windows Firewall?
answer: Go to Control Panel > System and Security > Windows Defender Firewall and click 'Turn Windows Defender Firewall on or off'. Make sure it's enabled for both private and public networks. You can also manage firewall rules to allow or block specific apps through 'Advanced settings'.

question: What is multi-factor authentication (MFA) and why is it important?
answer: MFA requires two or more verification factors to gain access: something you know (password), something you have (phone/token), and something you are (biometrics). Even if your password is stolen, MFA prevents unauthorized access because the attacker also needs the second factor. It's one of the most effective account security measures.

question: How do I perform a security audit on my personal devices?
answer: Update all software and operating systems. Review app permissions and revoke unnecessary ones. Check which apps have access to your accounts (Google, Facebook) and remove unfamiliar ones. Enable full-disk encryption. Review passwords in your password manager for weaknesses and reused passwords. Check haveibeenpwned.com for breached credentials.

question: What is HTTPS and how does SSL/TLS work?
answer: HTTPS secures web communication using TLS (Transport Layer Security). When you connect to an HTTPS site, the server presents its digital certificate to verify its identity. Your browser and the server negotiate encryption settings and exchange keys, establishing an encrypted tunnel for all data. The padlock icon in your browser confirms the connection is secure.

question: How do I spot a fake website or scam?
answer: Check the URL carefully for misspellings (e.g., 'paypa1.com') and ensure it starts with 'https'. Look for poor grammar, stock images, and no contact information. Verify the domain registration age using Whois. Search for reviews or scam reports about the site. When in doubt, access the site directly by typing the known URL rather than clicking a link.

question: What is data encryption and should I encrypt my hard drive?
answer: Data encryption scrambles data so it can only be read with the correct decryption key. Encrypting your hard drive (with BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on Mac, or LUKS on Linux) ensures data is unreadable if your device is lost or stolen. For laptops and devices containing sensitive information, full-disk encryption is strongly recommended.

question: What is a DDoS attack and how do organizations defend against it?
answer: A DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attack floods a server or network with traffic from many sources, making it unavailable to legitimate users. Defenses include traffic filtering, rate limiting, cloud-based DDoS protection services (like Cloudflare or AWS Shield), and having sufficient bandwidth headroom. Identifying and blocking attack traffic patterns is key.

question: What is a security certificate error and what should I do?
answer: A certificate error means your browser cannot verify the website's identity, often because the certificate is expired, invalid, or mismatched. Do not proceed to the site if you're not sure — it may be a sign of a man-in-the-middle attack. If it's a site you trust and manage yourself, the certificate may simply need renewal.

question: What is the Dark Web and should I be concerned about it?
answer: The Dark Web is a part of the internet accessible only through the Tor browser, used for both legitimate privacy purposes and illegal activities. Most people have no reason to access it. However, your data (passwords, credit card numbers) can end up for sale there after breaches. Monitor your credentials via services like haveibeenpwned.com and use unique passwords for each account.

question: What is endpoint security?
answer: Endpoint security protects individual devices (endpoints) like computers, laptops, and mobile phones that connect to a corporate network. It typically includes antivirus, EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response), data encryption, and patch management. As more employees work remotely, endpoint security has become critically important.

question: How do I safely dispose of an old computer with personal data?
answer: Before disposing, perform a secure wipe of your hard drive using tools like DBAN (for HDDs) or the manufacturer's secure erase for SSDs. Simply deleting files or formatting is not enough for sensitive data. For SSDs, the drive manufacturer's secure erase utility or the built-in factory reset with encryption enabled is recommended.

question: What is a security token or hardware key?
answer: A hardware security key (like a YubiKey) is a physical device that provides a second factor of authentication using cryptographic keys. It's plugged into a USB port or tapped on a phone. Unlike SMS-based 2FA, hardware keys are immune to phishing because they verify the website's legitimacy as part of the authentication process.

question: What is penetration testing?
answer: Penetration testing (pen testing) is an authorized simulated cyberattack performed to identify vulnerabilities in a system, network, or application. Security professionals use tools and techniques similar to real attackers to find weaknesses before malicious actors do. Pen testing results help organizations prioritize and fix security gaps.

question: How do I protect my children online?
answer: Enable parental controls in your router or operating system to filter content and set screen time limits. Use family-oriented DNS services like CleanBrowsing. Have regular open conversations with children about online safety. Monitor activity appropriately for age, and teach them never to share personal information with strangers online.

question: What is GDPR and why does it matter?
answer: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) is a European Union law governing how organizations collect, store, and process personal data. It gives individuals rights over their data (access, correction, deletion) and requires organizations to be transparent about data use. Non-compliance can result in large fines. Even non-EU companies must comply if they handle EU residents' data.

question: What are the most common types of malware?
answer: Common types include viruses (self-replicating code), worms (self-spreading across networks), trojans (disguised as legitimate software), ransomware (encrypts files for ransom), spyware (monitors activity), and adware (displays unwanted ads). Good antivirus software can detect and remove most types, but behavioral monitoring is increasingly important for newer threats.

question: How do I safely use public Wi-Fi?
answer: Avoid accessing sensitive accounts (banking, email) on public Wi-Fi. Use a VPN to encrypt your traffic. Ensure websites use HTTPS. Disable automatic Wi-Fi connection and file sharing on your device. Prefer mobile data for sensitive activities. Public Wi-Fi networks are prime targets for man-in-the-middle attacks.

question: How do I free up storage space on my iPhone?
answer: Go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage to see what's using the most space. You can offload unused apps (which removes the app but keeps its data), delete old videos and photos, and clear streaming app caches. Enabling iCloud Photos stores full-resolution photos in the cloud and keeps optimized versions on your device.

question: How do I factory reset my Android phone?
answer: Go to Settings > General Management (or System) > Reset > Factory Data Reset. This wipes all data, apps, and settings. Make sure to back up important data first via Google backup or manual transfer. If the phone is locked, most Android devices allow a factory reset from the recovery menu.

question: How do I back up my iPhone?
answer: Connect to Wi-Fi and go to Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > iCloud Backup, then tap 'Back Up Now'. Alternatively, connect to a Mac or PC and use Finder (macOS) or iTunes (Windows) for a local backup. iCloud automatically backs up daily when your phone is charging and connected to Wi-Fi.

question: How do I transfer data from Android to iPhone?
answer: Use Apple's 'Move to iOS' app, available on the Google Play Store. During iPhone setup, select 'Move Data from Android', open the app on your Android, and follow the steps to transfer contacts, messages, photos, and more. Perform this during initial iPhone setup for the best experience.

question: How do I extend my phone battery life?
answer: Reduce screen brightness or enable auto-brightness. Turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS when not in use. Enable battery saver mode. Close background apps (though this has diminishing returns on modern phones). Avoid charging to 100% or draining to 0% frequently — keeping charge between 20-80% prolongs battery health.

question: How do I update apps on Android?
answer: Open the Google Play Store app, tap your profile icon, select 'Manage apps & device', then tap 'Update all'. You can enable automatic updates by going to Play Store settings > Network preferences > Auto-update apps. Keeping apps updated ensures you have the latest features and security patches.

question: How do I set up fingerprint unlock on Android?
answer: Go to Settings > Biometrics and Security (exact path varies by manufacturer) > Fingerprint. You'll need to have a PIN, pattern, or password set up first. Follow the on-screen instructions to enroll your fingerprint by lifting and pressing your finger repeatedly on the sensor.

question: What should I do if my phone falls in water?
answer: Remove the phone from water immediately and power it off if it's still on. Dry it gently with a cloth. Do NOT use a hairdryer or put it in rice — these are ineffective or damaging. Place it in a dry environment for 48 hours before turning it back on. Many modern phones have IP67/IP68 ratings for water resistance.

question: How do I enable 'Do Not Disturb' on my iPhone?
answer: Swipe down from the top-right corner to open Control Center and tap the crescent moon icon. Or go to Settings > Focus > Do Not Disturb to customize schedules and allowed contacts. You can allow calls from specific people or repeat callers to break through while silencing other notifications.

question: How do I check mobile data usage on Android?
answer: Go to Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Data Usage. You can see total usage, usage by app, and set data usage warnings or limits. This helps you identify which apps are consuming the most data so you can adjust their background data settings.

question: How do I remove a virus from an Android phone?
answer: Uninstall recently installed suspicious apps from Settings > Apps. Run a reputable mobile security app like Malwarebytes or Bitdefender. If the problem persists, boot into Safe Mode (hold power button, then long-press 'Power off') to disable third-party apps and uninstall malicious ones. A factory reset is the last resort.

question: What is the difference between Android and iOS?
answer: Android is an open-source OS by Google used by multiple manufacturers, offering more customization, sideloading, and hardware variety. iOS is Apple's closed, proprietary OS exclusive to iPhone and iPad, known for tight hardware-software integration, strong privacy features, and a curated App Store. Both are excellent — the choice often depends on ecosystem preference.

question: How do I share my phone's internet connection (hotspot)?
answer: On Android, go to Settings > Network & Internet > Hotspot & Tethering and enable 'Wi-Fi hotspot'. On iPhone, go to Settings > Personal Hotspot and toggle it on. Set a strong password for the hotspot. Note that mobile hotspot usage counts against your data plan.

question: How do I force restart a frozen iPhone?
answer: For iPhone 8 and later: quickly press and release Volume Up, then Volume Down, then hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears. For iPhone 7: hold Volume Down and Sleep/Wake simultaneously. For older models: hold Home and Sleep/Wake. This performs a hard reset without erasing data.

question: How do I enable developer options on Android?
answer: Go to Settings > About Phone and tap 'Build number' seven times rapidly. You'll see a message saying 'You are now a developer'. Developer options will then appear in Settings, giving access to USB debugging, animation scale settings, and other advanced options.

question: How do I block a phone number on iPhone?
answer: Open the Phone app, go to Recents, and tap the info (i) icon next to the number. Scroll down and select 'Block this Caller'. To manage blocked numbers, go to Settings > Phone > Blocked Contacts. Blocked callers go directly to voicemail and cannot see when messages are delivered.

question: How do I recover deleted photos on Android?
answer: Check your Google Photos app — deleted photos stay in the Trash for 30 days and can be restored. If they're not in Trash, check your cloud backup service. Third-party data recovery apps may recover photos if they haven't been overwritten, but results are not guaranteed. Regular cloud backups are the best prevention.

question: What is NFC and what can I use it for?
answer: NFC (Near Field Communication) is a short-range wireless technology (a few centimeters) used for contactless payments (like Google Pay or Apple Pay), pairing Bluetooth devices, reading NFC tags, and transferring small amounts of data. Most modern smartphones have NFC built in.

question: How do I set up Face ID on iPhone?
answer: Go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode. Enter your passcode, then tap 'Set Up Face ID'. Hold your iPhone in portrait orientation and position your face in the frame, then move your head in a circle to capture different angles. You can also set up an alternate appearance for cases like different hairstyles or eyeglasses.

question: How do I clear cache on Android apps?
answer: Go to Settings > Apps, select the app you want to clear cache for, tap 'Storage', then 'Clear Cache'. This removes temporary files the app has stored, which can free up space and fix app glitches without deleting your personal data or settings.

question: How do I use screen mirroring from my phone to a TV?
answer: On Android, use the Cast or Smart View feature (swipe down from the notification bar) and select your Chromecast or Smart TV. On iPhone, use AirPlay by swiping down to Control Center and tapping Screen Mirroring, then selecting your Apple TV or AirPlay 2-compatible TV. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

question: How do I set up email on my iPhone?
answer: Go to Settings > Mail > Accounts > Add Account. Choose your email provider (Google, Yahoo, Outlook, etc.) or select 'Other' for custom IMAP/POP3 settings. Enter your email and password. For Gmail and other major providers, the Mail app will configure server settings automatically.

question: What is the App Clip / Instant App feature on mobile phones?
answer: App Clips (iOS) and Instant Apps (Android) let you use a portion of an app without fully installing it. They load instantly when triggered by NFC, QR codes, or links and are ideal for one-time tasks like parking payments, renting a scooter, or ordering food. No installation is required, saving storage space.

question: How do I improve my phone's GPS accuracy?
answer: Ensure location services are enabled and set to 'High Accuracy' mode on Android (Settings > Location > Mode). Make sure the app has location permissions. Go outside or near a window for better satellite signal. Restart the app or toggle airplane mode to refresh the GPS receiver.

question: How do I set parental controls on an iPhone for a child?
answer: Go to Settings > Screen Time > Turn On Screen Time. Set a Screen Time passcode different from the device passcode. Use 'Content & Privacy Restrictions' to limit app usage, content ratings, web browsing, and purchases. You can also set downtime schedules and app limits by category.

question: What is the difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
answer: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides virtualized computing resources like VMs and storage — e.g., AWS EC2. PaaS (Platform as a Service) provides a platform for developing and deploying apps without managing infrastructure — e.g., Heroku. SaaS (Software as a Service) delivers fully functional applications over the internet — e.g., Google Workspace or Salesforce.

question: How do I set up Google Workspace for my small business?
answer: Go to workspace.google.com and sign up, entering your business domain. Verify domain ownership by adding a TXT record to your DNS. Add users in the Admin Console and configure Gmail to use your custom domain. Google Workspace includes Gmail, Drive, Docs, Meet, and Calendar with business-grade features.

question: What is Microsoft 365 and what does it include?
answer: Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) is a subscription service that includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneNote, and OneDrive cloud storage. Plans range from personal to enterprise. Apps can be installed on up to 5 devices and files sync across all devices via OneDrive.

question: How do I recover a deleted file from OneDrive?
answer: Go to onedrive.com, sign in, and click 'Recycle bin' in the left panel. Select the file and click 'Restore'. Deleted files stay in the recycle bin for up to 30 days. For Microsoft 365 subscribers, version history is also available by right-clicking a file and selecting 'Version history'.

question: How do I share a Google Drive folder with someone?
answer: Right-click the folder in Google Drive and select 'Share'. Enter the recipient's email address and choose their permission level: Viewer, Commenter, or Editor. Click 'Send'. You can also generate a shareable link and set whether anyone with the link can view or edit.

question: What is cloud storage and how is it different from local storage?
answer: Cloud storage saves files on remote servers accessible via the internet, from any device. Local storage saves files on the device's hard drive or SSD. Cloud storage offers accessibility and automatic backup but requires internet access and a subscription for large amounts. Local storage is faster and available offline but can be lost if the device fails.

question: How do I set up multi-factor authentication for a Microsoft 365 account?
answer: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Users > Active Users, select a user and click 'Multi-factor authentication'. Enable MFA for the user and have them register at aka.ms/mfasetup by choosing an authentication method like the Microsoft Authenticator app, SMS, or a phone call.

question: What is Slack and how do I use it for team communication?
answer: Slack is a messaging platform for teams, organized into channels (group chats by topic) and direct messages. Install the app or use the web version, join your team's workspace, and participate in channels. Use @mentions to notify specific people, share files by dragging them in, and integrate with tools like Google Drive, Jira, and GitHub.

question: What is Salesforce and who uses it?
answer: Salesforce is the world's leading CRM (Customer Relationship Management) platform, used by sales, marketing, and customer service teams to manage customer interactions, leads, and deals. It offers modules for sales automation, marketing campaigns, service cases, and analytics. It's widely used by businesses of all sizes.

question: How do I create a Zoom meeting and invite participants?
answer: Log in to Zoom and click 'Schedule a Meeting'. Set the date, time, and duration, then click 'Save'. Copy the meeting link or invitation text and send it to participants via email or calendar invite. You can also start an instant meeting from the Zoom app and share the meeting ID directly.

question: How do I migrate email from Gmail to Outlook?
answer: In Outlook, go to File > Add Account and add your Gmail account using the IMAP settings. Once connected, drag emails from your Gmail folders to Outlook's local folders to copy them. For large migrations, tools like Google Takeout or Microsoft's email migration tools in the admin center offer more automated options.

question: What is AWS (Amazon Web Services) and what is it used for?
answer: AWS is Amazon's cloud computing platform offering over 200 services including computing (EC2), storage (S3), databases (RDS), AI/ML, and networking. Businesses use it to host websites, run applications, store data, and build scalable services without owning physical servers. AWS operates on a pay-as-you-go pricing model.

question: What is the difference between Dropbox, Google Drive, and OneDrive?
answer: All three offer cloud storage and file syncing. Google Drive integrates tightly with Google Workspace apps. OneDrive integrates with Microsoft 365 and Windows. Dropbox is platform-agnostic and known for reliable sync across all operating systems and devices. Choice often depends on your existing ecosystem (Google, Microsoft, or neither).

question: How do I restore a previous version of a file in SharePoint?
answer: Open SharePoint, navigate to the document library, and right-click the file. Select 'Version history' to see all saved versions with timestamps and who made changes. Click 'Restore' next to the version you want to revert to. SharePoint retains major versions by default; minor versions can be configured in library settings.

question: What is Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) and what is it used for?
answer: Azure Active Directory (now called Microsoft Entra ID) is Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service. Organizations use it to manage user accounts, control access to apps and resources (including Microsoft 365 and third-party SaaS apps), enforce MFA, and enable single sign-on (SSO). It's the foundation of identity management in Microsoft cloud environments.

question: How do I automate tasks using Microsoft Power Automate?
answer: Sign in to Power Automate (flow.microsoft.com) and click 'Create'. Choose a template or start from scratch with a trigger (e.g., 'When an email arrives') and add actions (e.g., 'Save attachment to OneDrive'). No coding is required for most workflows. Power Automate integrates with hundreds of Microsoft and third-party services.

question: What is a CDN (Content Delivery Network) and why is it used?
answer: A CDN is a network of geographically distributed servers that cache and deliver web content (images, scripts, videos) from the server closest to the user. This reduces latency and speeds up page load times. CDNs like Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, and Akamai also provide DDoS protection and improved availability.

question: How do I set up automatic backups to cloud storage?
answer: For Windows, OneDrive's PC Folder Backup can automatically sync Desktop, Documents, and Pictures folders. For Mac, iCloud Drive can do the same. Third-party tools like Backblaze or Acronis offer full system backups to the cloud. Configure backup frequency and retention policies based on how critical your data is.

question: What is serverless computing and how is it different from traditional cloud hosting?
answer: In serverless computing (e.g., AWS Lambda, Azure Functions), you run code without provisioning or managing servers — you only pay for execution time. Traditional cloud hosting (VMs or containers) requires you to manage and pay for server resources even when idle. Serverless is ideal for event-driven, irregular workloads.

question: What is single sign-on (SSO) and how does it benefit organizations?
answer: SSO allows users to authenticate once and access multiple applications without logging in again. It improves user experience by reducing password fatigue and simplifies IT management by centralizing authentication. It's implemented through identity providers (IdPs) like Azure AD, Okta, or Google using protocols like SAML or OAuth.

question: How do I export my data from a SaaS platform?
answer: Most SaaS platforms offer a data export option in account settings. For Google Workspace, use Google Takeout. For Salesforce, use the Data Export feature in the admin panel. Always export your data regularly in case you need to switch providers or the service becomes unavailable. Store exports in a secure, separate location.

question: What is Kubernetes and what problem does it solve?
answer: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration platform that automates deploying, scaling, and managing containerized applications. It solves the problem of running many containers across multiple servers reliably — automatically restarting failed containers, load balancing traffic, and rolling out updates without downtime.

question: How does cloud pricing work and how can I avoid surprise bills?
answer: Cloud providers charge based on resources consumed: compute time, storage, data transfer, and API calls. To avoid surprise bills, set up billing alerts and budget alarms (e.g., in AWS Cost Explorer). Use reserved instances or savings plans for predictable workloads. Review and shut down unused resources regularly.

question: What is Notion and how can I use it for productivity?
answer: Notion is an all-in-one workspace combining notes, wikis, databases, tasks, and project management. You can create pages with rich content, build relational databases for tracking projects or contacts, and share workspaces with teams. It's highly flexible — suitable for personal journaling, team knowledge bases, or complex project management.

question: What is Jira and how is it used in software development?
answer: Jira is a project management and issue-tracking tool widely used in agile software development. Teams create 'issues' (bugs, tasks, stories), organize them into sprints and epics, and track progress on kanban or scrum boards. Jira integrates with GitHub, Confluence, Slack, and many other developer tools.

question: My computer is running very slow. What should I do?
answer: Start by checking Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) for processes using high CPU or memory. Disable unnecessary startup programs and scan for malware. Ensure the hard drive isn't nearly full — keep at least 15% free. On older machines, upgrading to an SSD or adding more RAM provides the most significant performance improvement.

question: My PC won't turn on. What are the first steps to diagnose it?
answer: Check that the power cable is firmly connected and the outlet is working. For desktops, check that the PSU switch is in the 'on' position. Listen for any beep codes when you press power. Try a different power cable or outlet. If there's no response at all, the PSU may have failed.

question: Windows is stuck on the loading screen. How do I fix it?
answer: Force shut down by holding the power button for 5 seconds. On the next boot, Windows may enter Automatic Repair mode. If not, access Advanced Startup Options by holding Shift while clicking Restart. Try 'Startup Repair' or boot into Safe Mode to diagnose driver or software issues.

question: My computer is showing a blue screen of death (BSOD). What does it mean?
answer: A BSOD indicates a critical system error. Note the error code (e.g., DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL) and search it online. Common causes include faulty drivers, hardware issues, or corrupted system files. Run 'sfc /scannow' in an elevated Command Prompt to check for corrupted files and update or roll back recently installed drivers.

question: My Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting. How do I fix it?
answer: Update your wireless network adapter drivers. Go to Device Manager > Network Adapters, right-click your adapter, and select 'Update driver'. In adapter Properties > Power Management, uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. Try assigning a static IP or changing your router's Wi-Fi channel to reduce interference.

question: An application keeps crashing. How do I troubleshoot it?
answer: Update the application to the latest version. Reinstall it by uninstalling fully and reinstalling fresh. Check the Event Viewer (search in Start menu) > Windows Logs > Application for error codes. Run the app as administrator. If it uses Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables, reinstall those too.

question: My printer says 'offline'. How do I fix it?
answer: Open Settings > Devices > Printers & Scanners, click the printer, and select 'Open queue'. In the queue window, click Printer and uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'. Restart the printer and check all cable connections. If it persists, remove the printer, restart the Print Spooler service (in Services.msc), and re-add the printer.

question: My laptop battery drains very fast. What can I do?
answer: Reduce screen brightness and check Settings > Battery > Battery Usage to identify apps consuming excessive power. Disable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when not needed. Check battery health — on Windows use 'powercfg /batteryreport' in Command Prompt; on Mac check System Information > Power. If battery health is below 80%, consider replacement.

question: My keyboard keys are not working. How do I fix it?
answer: First, restart your computer — sometimes this resolves temporary issues. Check that keyboard drivers are current in Device Manager. Try the keyboard on another computer to see if it's a hardware issue. Clean under the keys with compressed air. If specific keys don't work, the keyboard may need replacement.

question: My monitor shows 'No Signal'. What should I check?
answer: Ensure the video cable is securely connected to both the monitor and GPU/motherboard. If using a docking station or adapter, test without it. Try a different port type (HDMI vs DisplayPort) or a different cable. If the PC is running but monitor shows no signal, the GPU may be failing or not seated properly.

question: How do I fix 'DNS server not responding' error?
answer: Open a Command Prompt as administrator and type 'ipconfig /flushdns'. Change your DNS servers to Google's (8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4) or Cloudflare's (1.1.1.1) in your network adapter properties. Restart your router. Disable then re-enable your network adapter. On rare occasions, your antivirus software can interfere with DNS resolution.

question: My PC makes a clicking noise from the hard drive. What does that mean?
answer: Clicking sounds from a hard drive often indicate imminent drive failure — this is serious. Immediately back up all important data. The clicking is typically caused by the read/write head struggling to find data. Run a S.M.A.R.T. test (using tools like CrystalDiskInfo) to assess drive health. Replace the drive as soon as possible.

question: How do I fix a frozen macOS app?
answer: Press Command + Option + Esc to open Force Quit. Select the frozen app and click 'Force Quit'. You can also right-click the app in the Dock and hold Option to see 'Force Quit'. If the entire system is unresponsive, press and hold the power button for 10 seconds to force a shutdown.

question: My phone screen is cracked but still works. Should I replace it immediately?
answer: A cracked screen can still function, but the cracks can spread and eventually damage the digitizer (touch layer) or LCD. If the crack exposes the internals, moisture can cause further damage. Most phone repair shops can replace the screen; cost varies by model. Applying a tempered glass screen protector can prevent further cracking in the short term.

question: How do I fix error code 0x80070057 in Windows?
answer: This error commonly occurs with Windows Update or when trying to format a disk. For Windows Update, run the Windows Update Troubleshooter in Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot. For disk formatting, the error may indicate file system corruption — run 'chkdsk /f' from an elevated Command Prompt on the affected drive.

question: My external hard drive is not showing up. How do I fix it?
answer: Try a different USB port or cable. Check Disk Management (right-click Start > Disk Management) — the drive may appear there but need a drive letter assigned or need initializing. Update USB and storage drivers in Device Manager. Test the drive on another computer to determine if it's a drive or PC issue.

question: How do I fix audio that suddenly stopped working in Windows?
answer: Right-click the speaker icon in the taskbar and run the Audio Troubleshooter. Check that the correct playback device is selected (right-click speaker icon > Open Sound settings). Check that the volume mixer doesn't have the app muted. Update audio drivers in Device Manager. Sometimes disabling then re-enabling the audio device resets it.

question: My laptop touchpad is not working. How do I fix it?
answer: Check that the touchpad isn't disabled by a function key combination (often Fn + F5 or similar, look for a touchpad icon). In Settings > Devices > Touchpad, ensure it's enabled. Update or reinstall the touchpad driver in Device Manager. If a USB mouse is connected, some systems disable the touchpad automatically.

question: Applications are taking a very long time to open. How do I speed them up?
answer: Check if the hard drive is nearly full — SSDs especially slow down when over 85% full. Malware can cause sluggish performance, so run a scan. Check if Windows is in the middle of updates in the background. If the system is old and uses a spinning HDD, upgrading to an SSD will dramatically improve application load times.

question: How do I fix 'This site can't be reached' in Chrome?
answer: Check your internet connection by visiting another site. Flush DNS with 'ipconfig /flushdns' in Command Prompt. Clear Chrome's browsing data (Ctrl+Shift+Delete). Disable Chrome extensions temporarily. Check your firewall or antivirus isn't blocking the site. If only specific sites are affected, the issue may be with those servers.

question: My phone won't charge. What should I try?
answer: Inspect the charging port for lint or debris and carefully clean it with a toothpick or compressed air. Try a different charging cable and adapter. Restart the phone. On Android, check battery settings to see if the device is overheating, which pauses charging. If using a wireless charger, ensure alignment is correct.

question: How do I fix a blurry or low-resolution display issue in Windows?
answer: Right-click the desktop, select Display settings, and set the resolution to the monitor's native resolution (usually labeled 'Recommended'). For blurry apps specifically, right-click the app's shortcut, go to Properties > Compatibility, and enable 'Override high DPI scaling behavior'. Update GPU drivers as well.

question: My Bluetooth device won't pair. How do I fix it?
answer: Make sure the Bluetooth device is in pairing mode (usually hold a button until the light flashes). On your computer, remove the device from Bluetooth settings and attempt to pair again fresh. Turn Bluetooth off and on. Update Bluetooth drivers. Ensure the device is within range and that no other device is currently connected to it.

question: How do I fix 'insufficient disk space' errors even when the disk appears to have space?
answer: Windows Temp files, the Recycle Bin, or system restore points may be taking up hidden space. Run Disk Cleanup and also clean system files from it. Use WinDirStat or TreeSize Free to visualize exactly what's consuming disk space. Large log files in C:\Windows\Logs can sometimes grow very large.

question: My webcam is not detected by my computer. How do I fix it?
answer: Check Device Manager for the webcam — if there's a yellow warning icon, right-click and update drivers. If the webcam doesn't appear at all, try a different USB port. Check privacy settings in Windows: Settings > Privacy > Camera must allow apps to access it. Test the webcam in a different application like the Camera app.

question: How do I fix OneDrive sync errors?
answer: Click the OneDrive icon in the system tray to see error details. Common issues include files with unsupported characters in names, files exceeding size limits, or storage being full. Reset OneDrive by running 'onedrive.exe /reset' from Run (Windows+R). Sign out and back in from the OneDrive settings.

question: My computer clock keeps losing time. How do I fix it?
answer: The CMOS battery on the motherboard may be dying — it's a small coin-cell battery (usually CR2032) that maintains the BIOS settings including the clock when the PC is off. Replace it (usually costs under $5) and reconfigure BIOS settings. Enable automatic time sync in Windows: Settings > Time & Language > Sync Now.

question: How do I fix slow internet speed on only one device when others are fine?
