answer: The issue is with that specific device. Update the network adapter drivers. Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network. Disable any VPN running on the device. Check for malware. In network adapter settings, set Speed & Duplex to 'Auto Negotiation'. On Wi-Fi, try moving closer to the router or switching frequency bands.

question: How do I fix a game that keeps crashing to desktop?
answer: Update your GPU and DirectX drivers. Verify the game's file integrity through Steam or Epic Games Launcher. Check that your PC meets the game's minimum requirements, especially VRAM. Lower in-game graphics settings. Monitor temperatures with HWiNFO to check for thermal throttling. Disable overclocking if applied.

question: How do I recover a Word document that wasn't saved?
answer: In Word, go to File > Info > Manage Document > Recover Unsaved Documents. Word autosaves drafts in a temp folder. Check C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Office\UnsavedFiles. On Mac, look in ~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Word/Data/Library/Preferences/AutoRecovery. Enable AutoSave and increase the autosave frequency to minimize future data loss.

question: How do I enable Hyper-V on Windows 10?
answer: Go to Control Panel > Programs > Turn Windows features on or off. Check 'Hyper-V' and click OK. Your PC must have a 64-bit processor with SLAT support and at least 4 GB RAM. Hyper-V is only available on Windows 10 Pro, Enterprise, or Education editions.

question: What is the difference between sleep, hibernate, and shutdown in Windows?
answer: Sleep saves your session to RAM and uses minimal power, resuming almost instantly. Hibernate saves the session to disk and uses no power, taking slightly longer to resume. Shutdown closes everything and uses no power. Use sleep for short breaks, hibernate for overnight, and shutdown for longer periods or updates.

question: How do I enable God Mode in Windows 10?
answer: Create a new folder on the desktop and rename it exactly to: GodMode.{ED7BA470-8E54-465E-825C-99712043E01C}. The folder icon will change to a Control Panel icon, giving you a single view of all Windows settings and administrative tools in one place.

question: How do I use the Windows Subsystem for Android?
answer: Install the Amazon Appstore from the Microsoft Store, which also installs Windows Subsystem for Android. Once set up, you can install and run Android apps on Windows 11. You can enable developer mode in WSA settings to sideload APK files directly.

question: What is Windows Sandbox and how do I use it?
answer: Windows Sandbox is a lightweight, isolated desktop environment for safely running untrusted software. Enable it in Windows Features (requires Windows 10/11 Pro). Each time you open Sandbox, it starts fresh — anything done inside is discarded when you close it, keeping your main system safe.

question: How do I change the default app for a file type in Windows?
answer: Right-click the file, select 'Open with' > 'Choose another app'. Select your preferred app and check 'Always use this app to open [file type] files'. You can also manage all file associations in Settings > Apps > Default Apps > Choose defaults by file type.

question: How do I reduce Windows update bandwidth usage?
answer: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > Advanced options > Delivery Optimization. You can limit the bandwidth used for downloading updates in the background and restrict how much bandwidth is used for uploading to other PCs.

question: What is the Windows Registry and what should I avoid changing?
answer: The Registry is a hierarchical database storing OS and application settings. Avoid deleting or modifying keys unless you know exactly what they do. Never edit the Registry while troubleshooting unless guided by a reliable source. Always export a backup of a key before changing it via File > Export in Registry Editor.

question: How do I set up a scheduled task in Windows?
answer: Open Task Scheduler from the Start menu. Click 'Create Basic Task', give it a name, set a trigger (daily, weekly, at startup), and specify the action (run a program, script, or URL). Advanced tasks can be created with 'Create Task' for more granular conditions and settings.

question: How do I change the language in Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > Time & Language > Language. Click 'Add a language', select your language, and download it. Set it as the display language and sign out/in for changes to take effect. You can also add keyboard input methods for multilingual typing.

question: What is a DLL file in Windows?
answer: A DLL (Dynamic Link Library) is a file containing code and data that can be used by multiple programs simultaneously. DLLs reduce code duplication and allow modular updates. 'DLL not found' errors occur when a program can't find the library it needs — reinstalling the app usually fixes this.

question: How do I check which version of .NET is installed on Windows?
answer: Open Command Prompt and run 'reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP /s /v Version'. For .NET 5+, run 'dotnet --list-runtimes' if the .NET CLI is installed. You can also check in Programs and Features for installed .NET Framework versions.

question: How do I enable automatic login in Windows 10?
answer: Press Windows+R and type 'netplwiz'. Uncheck 'Users must enter a user name and password to use this computer', click Apply, and enter your password when prompted. Note that automatic login reduces security, especially on portable devices.

question: What is the difference between FAT32, exFAT, and NTFS?
answer: FAT32 is widely compatible but limited to 4 GB max file size. exFAT removes the file size limit and works across Windows, macOS, and Linux — ideal for USB drives. NTFS supports large files, permissions, and journaling but has limited native write support on macOS without third-party software.

question: How do I use PowerShell to find large files?
answer: Open PowerShell and run: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 20 FullName, Length. This lists the 20 largest files on the C: drive. Adjust the path to search specific folders.

question: How do I enable clipboard history in Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > System > Clipboard and toggle 'Clipboard history' on. Press Windows+V to open the clipboard history panel, showing recently copied text, images, and HTML. You can pin frequently used items so they stay in the list permanently.

question: How do I repair Windows using the SFC tool?
answer: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run 'sfc /scannow'. This scans all protected system files and replaces corrupted ones with cached copies. If SFC reports errors it couldn't fix, follow up with 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' to repair the component store first.

question: What is a swap file or virtual memory in Windows?
answer: Virtual memory uses a portion of the hard drive as an extension of RAM when physical RAM is full. Windows manages the pagefile.sys automatically. You can customize it in System Properties > Advanced > Performance > Virtual Memory. Moving the pagefile to an SSD and increasing RAM are both options for improving performance.

question: How do I use Windows built-in backup?
answer: Go to Control Panel > Backup and Restore (Windows 7). Click 'Set up backup', choose a destination drive, and select what to back up. Windows can automatically back up files and create system images on a schedule. This is separate from File History, which tracks file version history.

question: How do I enable Night Light in Windows 10?
answer: Go to Settings > System > Display and toggle 'Night light' on. Click 'Night light settings' to adjust the color temperature and set a schedule, such as sunset to sunrise. Night Light reduces blue light emission, which may help reduce eye strain in low-light environments.

question: How do I use the Linux grep command?
answer: The grep command searches for patterns in text files. Basic syntax: 'grep pattern filename'. Use 'grep -r pattern /directory' to search recursively. 'grep -i' makes the search case-insensitive, and 'grep -n' shows line numbers. Combine with pipes: 'cat file.txt | grep error' to filter output.

question: What is the difference between apt and apt-get in Linux?
answer: apt is a newer, more user-friendly command that combines the most commonly used features of apt-get and apt-cache. apt-get is the older, more scriptable version. For interactive use, apt is preferred. For scripts, apt-get is still recommended for its stable interface.

question: How do I check disk I/O usage in Linux?
answer: Use 'iostat -x 1' (part of sysstat package) for real-time disk I/O statistics per device. The 'iotop' command shows disk I/O usage per process, similar to how top shows CPU usage. Install these tools with 'sudo apt install sysstat iotop'.

question: How do I set up SSH on a Linux server?
answer: Install OpenSSH server with 'sudo apt install openssh-server'. The service starts automatically. Check it's running with 'sudo systemctl status ssh'. Connect from another machine with 'ssh username@server-ip'. Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config to harden settings like disabling root login and password authentication.

question: What is a Linux init system and what is systemd?
answer: The init system is the first process run when Linux boots (PID 1), responsible for starting all other services. systemd is the modern init system used by most major distributions. Use 'systemctl start/stop/enable/disable servicename' to manage services. 'systemctl status servicename' shows current state and recent logs.

question: How do I monitor network traffic in Linux?
answer: Use 'netstat -tuln' to see listening ports and active connections, or the modern replacement 'ss -tuln'. Install 'nethogs' to see bandwidth usage per process. 'tcpdump' captures raw packets for analysis. For a graphical view, 'nload' or 'iftop' show real-time bandwidth usage per interface.

question: How do I manage packages with yum or dnf on Red Hat/CentOS/Fedora?
answer: Use 'dnf install packagename' to install, 'dnf remove packagename' to uninstall, and 'dnf update' to upgrade all packages. dnf replaced yum as the default package manager on Fedora and RHEL 8+. 'dnf search keyword' finds packages, and 'dnf info packagename' shows details about a package.

question: How do I configure network interfaces in Ubuntu using Netplan?
answer: Edit the YAML configuration file in /etc/netplan/ (e.g., /etc/netplan/00-installer-config.yaml). Define the interface name, whether to use DHCP or a static IP, and optional DNS settings. Run 'sudo netplan apply' to apply the configuration without rebooting.

question: How do I use the awk command in Linux?
answer: awk is a text processing tool for extracting and manipulating data. 'awk '{print $1}' file.txt' prints the first field of each line. 'awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd' uses colon as delimiter to print usernames. awk supports conditionals, loops, and arithmetic for complex text transformations.

question: What is SELinux and how does it affect my Linux system?
answer: SELinux (Security-Enhanced Linux) is a mandatory access control system that enforces security policies beyond standard Unix permissions. It can prevent processes from accessing files or network ports they shouldn't, even if standard permissions would allow it. 'getenforce' shows current mode; use 'setenforce permissive' to troubleshoot SELinux-related denials.

question: How do I create a bootable USB drive for Linux?
answer: Download the Linux distribution's ISO file. On Windows, use Rufus or balenaEtcher. On macOS or Linux, use balenaEtcher or the 'dd' command: 'sudo dd if=linux.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress' (replace /dev/sdX with your USB device). Double-check the device path before running dd to avoid overwriting the wrong disk.

question: How do I set up automatic updates on macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Software Update and check 'Automatically keep my Mac up to date'. Click 'Advanced' to configure which types of updates install automatically — including OS updates, app updates, and security responses. Keeping macOS updated is important for security and compatibility.

question: How do I use Spotlight Search on a Mac?
answer: Press Command+Space to open Spotlight. Type your search query to find files, apps, contacts, emails, web results, and more. Spotlight can also perform calculations, unit conversions, and dictionary lookups. You can configure which categories Spotlight searches in System Preferences > Spotlight.

question: What is macOS Gatekeeper and how does it work?
answer: Gatekeeper is a macOS security feature that prevents malicious software from running. By default, it only allows apps from the Mac App Store and identified developers. If you try to open an app blocked by Gatekeeper, right-click it and choose 'Open' to bypass the warning once. Adjust the setting in System Preferences > Security & Privacy.

question: How do I use Time Machine to restore a specific file on Mac?
answer: Open the folder where the file was located, then launch Time Machine from the Menu Bar or Applications. Use the timeline on the right to go back to a date when the file existed. Select the file and click 'Restore' to bring it back. Time Machine restores the file to its original location.

question: What is Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon Macs?
answer: Rosetta 2 is a translation layer that allows apps built for Intel Macs to run on Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3) Macs. It translates x86_64 instructions to ARM at install time or first launch. Most Intel apps work transparently through Rosetta 2. Developers can rebuild apps as Universal Binaries to run natively on both architectures.

question: How do I free up RAM on macOS?
answer: macOS manages RAM automatically using memory compression and swapping. To free up RAM, quit apps you're not using — use Command+Q to fully quit rather than just closing windows. You can use the 'purge' command in Terminal to flush disk cache. Adding more physical RAM is the most effective long-term solution.

question: How do I use the macOS Terminal to navigate directories?
answer: Use 'cd directory_name' to enter a folder, 'cd ..' to go up one level, and 'cd ~' to go to your home directory. 'ls' lists files, 'ls -la' shows hidden files and details. 'pwd' prints the current directory path. 'mkdir foldername' creates a new directory.

question: What is the difference between POP3 and IMAP for email?
answer: POP3 downloads emails to your device and typically deletes them from the server — useful if you only access email from one device. IMAP keeps emails on the server and syncs across all devices, making it better for multi-device access. Most modern email clients and services default to IMAP.

question: How do I convert a PDF to Word document format?
answer: Microsoft Word (2013 and later) can open PDF files and convert them — just open the file in Word. Adobe Acrobat's Export PDF feature is the most accurate option. Free online tools like Smallpdf, ILovePDF, and Adobe's online tools can also convert PDFs to DOCX format, though complex formatting may not convert perfectly.

question: What is a VirtualBox Guest Additions and how do I install it?
answer: Guest Additions is a package of drivers and utilities installed inside a VirtualBox VM that improves performance and enables features like shared folders, shared clipboard, drag-and-drop, and automatic window resizing. In VirtualBox with the VM running, go to Devices > Insert Guest Additions CD image and run the installer inside the VM.

question: How do I use the diff command in Linux?
answer: The 'diff file1.txt file2.txt' command shows the differences between two files. Lines preceded by '<' are from file1, and '>' from file2. Use 'diff -u' for unified format, which is easier to read. 'diff -r dir1 dir2' compares two directories recursively.

question: What is a shell script and how do I run one in Linux?
answer: A shell script is a text file containing a sequence of shell commands. Create one by starting the file with '#!/bin/bash', adding your commands, and saving with a .sh extension. Make it executable with 'chmod +x script.sh', then run it with './script.sh'. Scripts automate repetitive tasks.

question: How do I zip and unzip files on macOS?
answer: To zip a file or folder in Finder, right-click it and select 'Compress'. To unzip, double-click the .zip file. In Terminal, use 'zip -r archive.zip folder/' to create a zip and 'unzip archive.zip' to extract. macOS also supports .tar.gz archives via the 'tar' command.

question: What is the Windows Group Policy Editor and who can use it?
answer: The Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) lets administrators configure Windows settings centrally, such as password policies, software restrictions, and user permissions. It's available on Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise, and Education editions. Home edition users can achieve similar results through Registry edits. Access it via Run > gpedit.msc.

question: How do I set up printer sharing on a Windows network?
answer: On the PC with the printer, go to Settings > Devices > Printers & Scanners, select the printer, click Manage, then 'Printer properties'. Go to the Sharing tab and check 'Share this printer'. On the other PC, go to Printers & Scanners > Add a printer > select the shared printer from the network.

question: How do I use the Windows Task Scheduler to run a Python script?
answer: Open Task Scheduler and create a new task. Set the trigger (e.g., daily at a specific time). For the action, set the program to 'python.exe' (or the full path), and the argument to the script path (e.g., C:\scripts\myscript.py). Ensure the task runs under an account with the necessary permissions.

question: What is the difference between a 32-bit and 64-bit application?
answer: A 32-bit application can access up to 4 GB of RAM regardless of how much the system has, while a 64-bit application can access significantly more. On 64-bit Windows, both can run. 32-bit apps are stored in C:\Program Files (x86). For best performance, use 64-bit versions when available.

question: How do I use the Windows Event Viewer?
answer: Open Event Viewer by searching in the Start menu. Navigate to Windows Logs > Application, Security, or System to see event logs. Each event has an ID, source, and description. Filter events by level (Error, Warning, Information) to find issues. Event IDs can be searched online for detailed explanations.

question: How do I set up a LAMP stack on Ubuntu?
answer: Install Apache with 'sudo apt install apache2', MySQL with 'sudo apt install mysql-server', and PHP with 'sudo apt install php libapache2-mod-php php-mysql'. Restart Apache with 'sudo systemctl restart apache2'. Test PHP by creating /var/www/html/info.php with '<?php phpinfo(); ?>'.

question: What is Docker and how is it different from a virtual machine?
answer: Docker runs applications in lightweight containers that share the host OS kernel, making them faster and more resource-efficient than VMs. VMs include a full OS per instance. Docker containers are portable — a Dockerized app runs the same on any machine with Docker installed. Use Docker for app deployment; VMs for full OS isolation.

question: How do I list all installed packages on Ubuntu?
answer: Run 'dpkg --list' or 'apt list --installed' in the terminal to see all installed packages. Use 'dpkg --list | grep packagename' to search for a specific package. 'apt show packagename' gives detailed information about a specific installed package.

question: How do I configure a static hostname in Linux?
answer: Edit /etc/hostname with your preferred hostname. Also update /etc/hosts to map the new hostname to 127.0.0.1. Run 'sudo hostnamectl set-hostname newhostname' to change it immediately without rebooting. Verify with 'hostname' command.

question: What is the purpose of the /etc/fstab file in Linux?
answer: The /etc/fstab file defines how disk partitions, filesystems, and remote filesystems (NFS, Samba) are automatically mounted at boot. Each line specifies the device, mount point, filesystem type, mount options, and backup/check settings. Errors in fstab can prevent the system from booting — always test with 'sudo mount -a' before rebooting.

question: How do I check open ports on a Linux system?
answer: Use 'ss -tuln' or 'netstat -tuln' to list all listening TCP and UDP ports with the associated process. 'sudo lsof -i :portnumber' shows which process is using a specific port. 'nmap localhost' performs a port scan of the local machine (requires nmap installation).

question: What is the difference between hard links and symbolic links in Linux?
answer: A hard link is a direct reference to the same inode (data on disk) — deleting the original file leaves the link intact. A symbolic (soft) link is a pointer to the file path — if the original is deleted, the symlink breaks. Create hard links with 'ln file link' and symlinks with 'ln -s target linkname'.

question: How do I set up a cron job to run every 5 minutes?
answer: Run 'crontab -e' and add the line: '*/5 * * * * /path/to/command'. The */5 syntax means 'every 5 minutes'. Ensure the command is executable and uses absolute paths, since cron runs in a minimal environment without your shell's PATH variable.

question: How do I check memory usage per process in Linux?
answer: Use 'ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -20' to list the top 20 processes by memory usage. 'top' or 'htop' shows real-time memory per process. '/proc/meminfo' contains detailed system-wide memory statistics. 'smem' provides more accurate memory accounting by considering shared memory.

question: How do I install Wine on Ubuntu to run Windows apps?
answer: Add the WineHQ repository and install wine with 'sudo apt install wine'. Run a Windows executable with 'wine program.exe'. Use 'winecfg' to configure the Wine environment. PlayOnLinux and Bottles are graphical frontends that make managing Wine prefixes easier.

question: How do I enable the root account on macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Users & Groups > Login Options, click 'Join' next to Network Account Server, then 'Open Directory Utility'. In Directory Utility, go to Edit > Enable Root User and set a password. Note: using the root account is generally discouraged; use 'sudo' for administrative tasks instead.

question: How do I use iCloud Drive on a Windows PC?
answer: Download iCloud for Windows from the Microsoft Store or Apple's website. Sign in with your Apple ID and select which iCloud features to sync, including iCloud Drive. Your iCloud Drive files appear in File Explorer under 'iCloud Drive'. Files marked with a cloud icon are stored only in iCloud and need to be downloaded.

question: What is Windows Defender Application Guard?
answer: Windows Defender Application Guard runs Microsoft Edge in an isolated Hyper-V container, so malicious websites cannot access your main OS. Enable it in Windows Features (requires Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise, or Education). It's particularly useful for enterprise environments where users may browse untrusted sites.

question: How do I change the default shell in Linux?
answer: Use 'chsh -s /bin/zsh' (or your preferred shell path) to change your default login shell. You'll need to log out and back in for the change to take effect. Find available shells in /etc/shells. 'echo $SHELL' shows your current shell.

question: How do I use rsync to back up files in Linux?
answer: Basic rsync: 'rsync -avz /source/ /destination/'. The -a flag preserves permissions and timestamps, -v is verbose, -z compresses during transfer. For remote backup over SSH: 'rsync -avz /local/path/ user@server:/remote/path/'. Add --delete to remove files from the destination that no longer exist in the source.

question: What is a kernel panic in Linux and what causes it?
answer: A kernel panic is a fatal error from which the Linux kernel cannot recover, similar to a Windows BSOD. Causes include hardware failures (bad RAM, overheating), corrupted kernel modules, or incompatible drivers. Check /var/log/kern.log or use 'journalctl -k' for kernel messages to diagnose the cause.

question: How do I use the sed command in Linux?
answer: sed (stream editor) modifies text in a file or stream. 'sed 's/old/new/g' file.txt' replaces all occurrences of 'old' with 'new'. Use '-i' to edit the file in place: 'sed -i 's/error/warning/g' log.txt'. sed also supports deleting lines, inserting text, and applying complex regex patterns.

question: How do I set up two-factor authentication for SSH login?
answer: Install Google Authenticator PAM module: 'sudo apt install libpam-google-authenticator'. Run 'google-authenticator' as the user to generate a QR code. Edit /etc/pam.d/sshd to add 'auth required pam_google_authenticator.so'. Set 'ChallengeResponseAuthentication yes' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart SSH.

question: How do I find which process is using a specific port in Windows?
answer: Open Command Prompt and run 'netstat -ano | findstr :portnumber'. Note the PID in the last column. Then open Task Manager > Details tab and find the process with that PID. Alternatively, run 'Get-Process -Id (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort portnumber).OwningProcess' in PowerShell.

question: How do I create a Windows system restore point?
answer: Search for 'Create a restore point' in the Start menu. In System Properties, click 'Create', give it a name, and click OK. Windows creates a snapshot of system files and registry. If something goes wrong later, go to the same panel and click 'System Restore' to revert to this point.

question: What is Git and how do I set it up on Windows?
answer: Git is a distributed version control system for tracking code changes. Download and install Git from git-scm.com. After installation, open Git Bash and configure your identity: 'git config --global user.name Your Name' and 'git config --global user.email you@example.com'. Use 'git init' to start tracking a project.

question: How do I enable Windows 11 on unsupported hardware?
answer: Microsoft provides workarounds via Registry edits to bypass TPM 2.0 and CPU checks. Add a registry key under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\Setup\MoSetup with value AllowUpgradesWithUnsupportedTPMOrCPU set to 1. Note that Microsoft doesn't officially support or guarantee updates for unsupported hardware.

question: How do I use the find command to run actions on files in Linux?
answer: Use 'find /path -name pattern -exec command {} \;' to execute a command on each found file. Example: 'find /tmp -name *.log -exec rm {} \;' deletes all .log files in /tmp. Use '-mtime +30' to find files older than 30 days. 'find . -type f -size +100M' finds files larger than 100 MB.

question: What is POSIX and why does it matter?
answer: POSIX (Portable Operating System Interface) is a set of standards defining how operating systems should behave, ensuring compatibility of software across Unix-like systems. Applications written to POSIX standards run on Linux, macOS, and other Unix systems without modification. It defines APIs, command-line utilities, and shell behavior.

question: How do I install and use Homebrew on macOS?
answer: Install Homebrew by running the official command from brew.sh in Terminal. Once installed, 'brew install packagename' installs CLI tools and software. 'brew install --cask appname' installs GUI apps. 'brew update && brew upgrade' keeps everything current. 'brew doctor' diagnoses issues with your installation.

question: How do I pin taskbar items in Windows 11?
answer: Right-click an open application in the taskbar and select 'Pin to taskbar'. To pin from the Start menu, right-click the app tile and choose 'Pin to taskbar'. To reorder pinned apps, drag them along the taskbar. Right-click a pinned icon and select 'Unpin from taskbar' to remove it.

question: How do I use the Windows 'robocopy' command?
answer: Robocopy (Robust File Copy) is an advanced file copy utility. Basic usage: 'robocopy source destination /e' copies all subdirectories including empty ones. Add /mir to mirror the source (deletes from destination what's no longer in source). /z enables restartable mode for large file transfers. It's more reliable than xcopy for large backup jobs.

question: What is BIOS vs UEFI and what is Secure Boot?
answer: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is the older firmware interface that initializes hardware and boots the OS. UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) is the modern replacement offering faster boot, support for drives larger than 2 TB, and a graphical interface. Secure Boot is a UEFI feature that prevents unauthorized bootloaders and malware from loading during startup.

question: How do I use Spotlight in macOS to quickly open apps?
answer: Press Command+Space to open Spotlight and start typing the app name. Spotlight shows matches as you type — press Enter to open the top result or use arrow keys to select. This is faster than navigating to the Applications folder. Spotlight also searches files, emails, contacts, and the web simultaneously.

question: How do I check and repair disk errors on macOS?
answer: Open Disk Utility from Applications > Utilities. Select your disk or partition and click 'First Aid', then 'Run'. Disk Utility checks for and repairs filesystem errors. For the startup disk, boot from macOS Recovery (Command+R at startup) and run First Aid from there.

question: How do I set up a RAID array in macOS using Disk Utility?
answer: Open Disk Utility and choose Edit > RAID Assistant. Select the RAID type (Mirrored for redundancy, Striped for performance, or Concatenated). Add the disks you want to include and give the RAID set a name. Note that Disk Utility's RAID is software-based, and Apple Silicon Macs do not support all RAID configurations.

question: How do I use the macOS 'defaults' command?
answer: The 'defaults' command lets you read and write macOS preference files from the Terminal. Example: 'defaults write com.apple.dock autohide-delay -float 0' removes the Dock auto-hide delay. 'defaults read com.apple.finder' shows all Finder preferences. After changing defaults, restart the app with 'killall Dock' or 'killall Finder'.

question: How do I disable System Integrity Protection (SIP) on macOS?
answer: Boot into macOS Recovery (Command+R for Intel Macs or hold power on Apple Silicon). Open Terminal from the Utilities menu and run 'csrutil disable'. Restart your Mac. SIP protects core system files from modification — only disable it if you have a specific technical need and understand the security implications.

question: What is the macOS Keychain and how do I manage it?
answer: The Keychain stores passwords, certificates, and keys securely. Open Keychain Access from Applications > Utilities to view, add, or delete stored items. If you're locked out of a Keychain, you can reset your login keychain in Keychain Access > Keychain Access menu > Preferences > Reset My Default Keychain. Safari and other apps automatically save to Keychain.

question: How do I migrate data from one Mac to another using Migration Assistant?
answer: On the new Mac, open Migration Assistant from Applications > Utilities. On the old Mac, also open Migration Assistant. Connect both Macs via Thunderbolt, USB-C cable, or ensure they're on the same Wi-Fi network. Follow the prompts to transfer user accounts, apps, and files. The process can take from minutes to hours depending on data size.

question: How do I enable SSH on macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Sharing and check 'Remote Login'. This starts the SSH daemon and allows SSH access. The dialog shows the SSH command to connect. Restrict access to specific users by selecting 'Only these users' and adding them. You can also enable SSH via Terminal with 'sudo systemsetup -setremotelogin on'.

question: What is the difference between .app and .dmg files on macOS?
answer: A .dmg (Disk Image) is a container file that mounts as a virtual disk — it usually contains a .app file that you drag to the Applications folder. A .app is a self-contained application bundle (actually a folder with a specific structure). Some .dmg files include a PKG installer instead of a .app.

question: How do I use macOS Automator to automate tasks?
answer: Open Automator from Applications. Choose a workflow type (Application, Quick Action, Folder Action, etc.). Use the library panel on the left to drag actions into the workflow. For example, create a workflow that resizes images in bulk: add 'Get Specified Finder Items', then 'Scale Images'. Save and run. No coding required.

question: How do I use Homebrew Cask to install macOS applications?
answer: After installing Homebrew, use 'brew install --cask appname' to install GUI applications. For example, 'brew install --cask google-chrome' installs Chrome. 'brew list --cask' shows installed casks. 'brew upgrade --cask' updates all cask applications. This is convenient for keeping software up to date from the command line.

question: How do I configure sudoers in Linux?
answer: Edit the sudoers file safely using 'sudo visudo', which validates syntax before saving. Add a line like 'username ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' to grant passwordless sudo to a user. Grant specific command access: 'username ALL=(ALL) /usr/bin/apt'. Never edit /etc/sudoers directly with a text editor — a syntax error can lock you out.

question: What is a Linux container (LXC) and how is it different from Docker?
answer: LXC (Linux Containers) provides OS-level virtualization running a full Linux userspace within a container. Docker (which originally used LXC) focuses on single-application containers with its own image format and ecosystem. LXC containers behave more like lightweight VMs; Docker containers are designed to run a single process or service.

question: How do I resize a partition in Linux without losing data?
answer: Use GParted (graphical) or parted (command line) to resize partitions. You can shrink NTFS or ext4 partitions, but the filesystem must be unmounted. Boot from a live USB with GParted, right-click the partition, and choose 'Resize/Move'. For the root partition, always back up first as mistakes can result in data loss.

question: How do I use the 'screen' or 'tmux' command to keep processes running after logout?
answer: Both screen and tmux are terminal multiplexers. Start a session with 'screen' or 'tmux'. Run your command, then detach from screen with Ctrl+A D or from tmux with Ctrl+B D. Log out — the process continues. Re-attach with 'screen -r' or 'tmux attach'. Tmux is more modern and feature-rich.

question: How do I view and kill processes in macOS Terminal?
answer: Use 'ps aux' to list all processes or 'top' for real-time view. Find a process by name with 'pgrep processname'. Kill it with 'kill PID' for a graceful stop or 'kill -9 PID' to force kill. 'pkill processname' kills by name. Activity Monitor provides the same functionality graphically.

question: How do I install fonts on Windows 10?
answer: Download the font file (.ttf or .otf). Right-click the file and select 'Install' to install for the current user, or 'Install for all users' to make it available system-wide. Fonts are stored in C:\Windows\Fonts. After installation, the font appears in all applications that list available fonts.

question: What is Windows Preinstallation Environment (WinPE)?
answer: WinPE is a minimal Windows environment used for deploying, troubleshooting, and repairing Windows installations. It boots from a USB drive or network and provides access to Command Prompt, disk tools, and recovery utilities. IT professionals use WinPE for imaging computers, running diagnostics, and repairing unbootable systems.

question: How do I change the default save location in Windows?
answer: Go to Settings > System > Storage > Change where new content is saved. Here you can set the default location for apps, documents, music, pictures, and videos to a different drive. This is especially useful if you have a small SSD for the OS and a larger drive for data storage.

question: How do I use the Windows XPS viewer?
answer: XPS (XML Paper Specification) is Microsoft's alternative to PDF. Open an XPS file by double-clicking it — Windows includes a built-in XPS Viewer. You can print to XPS from any application using the 'Microsoft XPS Document Writer' printer. Edge browser can also open XPS files. For wider compatibility, convert XPS to PDF using online tools.

question: How do I use PowerShell to manage services?
answer: Use 'Get-Service' to list all services and their status. 'Start-Service servicename' and 'Stop-Service servicename' control services. 'Set-Service -Name servicename -StartupType Automatic' sets startup type. For remote management, add '-ComputerName hostname' to most cmdlets.

question: How do I enable disk quotas in Windows?
answer: Open File Explorer, right-click a drive (must be NTFS), select Properties > Quota tab. Check 'Enable quota management'. Set a default limit and warning level. You can also set per-user limits by clicking 'Quota Entries'. Disk quotas prevent single users from consuming all available disk space on a shared system.

question: What is Windows LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution)?
answer: Windows LAPS is a Microsoft tool that automatically manages and rotates the local administrator password on domain-joined computers. Passwords are stored in Active Directory and are unique per device, reducing the risk of lateral movement attacks where attackers use one shared local admin password across many machines.

question: How do I use curl to test an API endpoint?
answer: Use 'curl -X GET https://api.example.com/endpoint' for a GET request. For POST with JSON data: 'curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key":"value"}' https://api.example.com/endpoint'. Add '-v' for verbose output and '-o filename' to save the response to a file.

question: How do I install Python on Windows?
answer: Download the installer from python.org. During installation, check 'Add Python to PATH' before clicking Install. Verify with 'python --version' in Command Prompt. Use 'pip install packagename' to install libraries. Consider using Python virtual environments ('python -m venv env') to isolate project dependencies.

question: What is an ISO file and how do I mount it in Windows?
answer: An ISO file is a disk image containing the exact contents of a CD, DVD, or Blu-ray. In Windows 10/11, double-click an ISO to mount it as a virtual drive — it appears as a new drive letter in File Explorer. Right-click and 'Eject' to unmount it. ISOs are commonly used for OS installation media and software distribution.

question: How do I use Hyper-V to create a virtual machine on Windows?
answer: Open Hyper-V Manager from the Start menu. Click 'New > Virtual Machine' in the right panel. Follow the wizard to set the name, generation (Gen 2 for modern OSes), memory, network, and virtual hard disk. Attach an ISO for OS installation. Start the VM and complete the OS setup as on a physical machine.

question: How do I set up Windows Hello for passwordless login?
answer: Go to Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options. Under Windows Hello, set up either Face recognition, Fingerprint, or PIN. Each method requires compatible hardware. Once configured, you can sign in with just your face, fingerprint, or a short PIN instead of typing your full password.

question: What is the difference between a local account and a Microsoft account in Windows?
answer: A local account exists only on your PC and doesn't sync settings or data to other devices. A Microsoft account (using an email) syncs settings, passwords, and OneDrive files across all your Windows devices and provides access to the Microsoft Store. You can switch between them in Settings > Accounts.

question: How do I use DISM to service Windows images?
answer: DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management) manages Windows image files. 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' repairs Windows component store corruption by downloading files from Windows Update. 'DISM /Online /Get-Packages' lists installed packages. DISM is often used before or after running SFC to fix stubborn system file issues.

question: How do I enable and configure Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2)?
answer: Run 'wsl --install' in PowerShell as administrator to install WSL2 with Ubuntu. Set WSL2 as default with 'wsl --set-default-version 2'. Install other distros with 'wsl --install -d DistroName'. WSL2 runs a real Linux kernel in a lightweight VM, offering better filesystem performance and full system call compatibility compared to WSL1.

question: How do I use the Windows 'netsh' command?
answer: netsh (Network Shell) configures network settings. 'netsh interface ip show config' displays IP settings. 'netsh wlan show profiles' lists saved Wi-Fi networks. 'netsh wlan show profile name=WiFiName key=clear' reveals the saved Wi-Fi password. 'netsh int ip reset' resets TCP/IP stack to fix network issues.

question: How do I configure Windows Defender Firewall rules?
answer: Open Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security from the Start menu. Click 'Inbound Rules' or 'Outbound Rules', then 'New Rule'. Choose rule type (Program, Port, Predefined, or Custom). Specify the program or port, choose Allow or Block, and select which network profiles the rule applies to. Name and save the rule.

question: What is the Windows 'hosts' file and how do I edit it?
answer: The hosts file (C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts) maps hostnames to IP addresses, overriding DNS. It's used to block websites (point to 127.0.0.1) or redirect domains for development. Edit it with Notepad run as administrator. Changes take effect immediately. Be cautious — malware sometimes modifies the hosts file.

question: How do I use PowerShell remoting?
answer: Enable remoting on the remote computer with 'Enable-PSRemoting -Force'. Connect from your machine with 'Enter-PSSession -ComputerName hostname -Credential user'. You can run commands on the remote machine as if you were there. For bulk operations, 'Invoke-Command -ComputerName host1,host2 -ScriptBlock {commands}' is used.

question: How do I find my product key for Windows?
answer: Run 'wmic path softwarelicensingservice get OA3xOriginalProductKey' in Command Prompt to retrieve the OEM key embedded in the firmware. For retail keys stored in the registry, use a third-party tool like ProduKey or ShowKeyPlus. Note that Windows 10/11 activations are now tied to your Microsoft account rather than a static key.

question: How do I use the Linux 'ps' command to find zombie processes?
answer: A zombie process has finished but its parent hasn't acknowledged its exit. Run 'ps aux | grep Z' to find zombie processes (they show 'Z' in the STAT column). Zombies can't be killed directly — kill the parent process instead, which causes them to be cleaned up. Persistent zombies indicate a bug in the parent application.

question: How do I configure log rotation in Linux?
answer: Log rotation is handled by logrotate, configured in /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d/. Each config file specifies the log path, rotation frequency (daily, weekly, monthly), number of files to keep, compression, and post-rotation scripts. Run 'sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf' to force rotation manually.

question: What is the difference between /dev/sda and /dev/nvme0n1 in Linux?
answer: '/dev/sda' refers to SATA or SAS drives (sda = first, sdb = second, etc.). '/dev/nvme0n1' refers to NVMe SSDs connected via PCIe (nvme0 = first controller, n1 = first namespace). Partitions are '/dev/sda1', '/dev/sda2' for SATA and '/dev/nvme0n1p1', '/dev/nvme0n1p2' for NVMe.

question: How do I use the Linux 'strace' command for debugging?
answer: strace traces system calls made by a process. 'strace command' runs a command with tracing. 'strace -p PID' attaches to a running process. It's useful for diagnosing why a program fails — you can see which files it tries to open, which syscalls fail, and what network connections it makes. Use '-e trace=file' to filter to file-related calls only.

question: How do I mount a Samba share in Linux?
answer: Install cifs-utils with 'sudo apt install cifs-utils'. Mount with: 'sudo mount -t cifs //server/sharename /mnt/point -o username=user,password=pass'. For auto-mounting at boot, add the entry to /etc/fstab with 'credentials=/etc/samba/creds' pointing to a file with username/password to avoid storing them in plaintext in fstab.

question: How do I use the 'lsof' command in Linux?
answer: lsof (list open files) shows all files opened by processes. 'lsof /path/to/file' shows which process has that file open. 'lsof -i :80' shows processes using port 80. 'lsof -u username' lists all files opened by a user. It's invaluable for troubleshooting 'device busy' errors and understanding what a process is doing.

question: How do I check and set system timezone in Linux?
answer: Run 'timedatectl' to see current timezone and NTP sync status. Set timezone with 'sudo timedatectl set-timezone Region/City' (e.g., 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur'). List all available timezones with 'timedatectl list-timezones'. The timezone is stored in /etc/localtime as a symlink to the appropriate zone file.

question: How do I compile a C program in Linux?
answer: Install GCC with 'sudo apt install build-essential'. Compile with 'gcc -o outputname sourcefile.c'. For multiple source files: 'gcc -o program file1.c file2.c'. Add '-Wall' for all warnings and '-g' for debug symbols. Run the compiled program with './outputname'. Makefiles automate the build process for larger projects.

question: How do I use 'iptables' to create a basic firewall in Linux?
answer: Allow established connections: 'iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT'. Allow SSH: 'iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT'. Drop everything else: 'iptables -A INPUT -j DROP'. Save rules with 'iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4'. Most modern systems use nftables or firewalld instead.

question: How do I use the macOS 'diskutil' command?
answer: 'diskutil list' shows all disks and partitions. 'diskutil info /dev/disk0' gives details about a disk. 'diskutil eraseDisk APFS DiskName /dev/disk2' formats a disk. 'diskutil mountDisk /dev/disk2' mounts all partitions on a disk. 'diskutil repairVolume /dev/disk0s2' runs a filesystem repair.

question: How do I use macOS launchd to schedule tasks?
answer: Create a .plist file in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ (user) or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ (system). Define the label, program path, and schedule using StartCalendarInterval or StartInterval keys. Load with 'launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.task.plist'. launchctl is the macOS equivalent of cron and systemctl combined.

question: What is APFS and how does it differ from HFS+?
answer: APFS (Apple File System) is Apple's modern filesystem introduced in 2017, replacing HFS+. APFS supports native encryption, snapshots, space sharing between volumes, and is optimized for SSDs. HFS+ was designed for spinning disks and lacks these features. Macs with macOS High Sierra or later automatically use APFS on SSDs.

question: How do I use iCloud Keychain on macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Apple ID > iCloud and enable Keychain. Safari will then offer to save and autofill passwords stored in iCloud Keychain, synced across all your Apple devices. Manage saved passwords in Safari > Preferences > Passwords or in the Passwords app (macOS Monterey and later).

question: How do I use Boot Camp to run Windows on a Mac?
answer: Open Boot Camp Assistant from Applications > Utilities. Provide a Windows ISO file and allocate disk space for the Windows partition. Boot Camp partitions your drive, installs Windows, and provides drivers. Hold Option at startup to choose between macOS and Windows. Note: Boot Camp is not available on Apple Silicon Macs.

question: How do I fix 'command not found' errors in Linux Terminal?
answer: The command either isn't installed or isn't in your PATH. Check with 'which commandname' or 'type commandname'. Install missing tools with apt, dnf, or your package manager. If the tool is installed but not found, add its directory to PATH: 'export PATH=$PATH:/path/to/bin' in your ~/.bashrc. Run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply.

question: How do I run a Windows application as a different user?
answer: Hold Shift and right-click the application, then select 'Run as different user'. Enter the username and password of the account you want to use. Alternatively, in Command Prompt: 'runas /user:domain\username "C:\path\to\app.exe"'. This is useful for running applications with admin rights without logging in as admin.

question: How do I use PowerShell to work with CSV files?
answer: Import a CSV with '$data = Import-Csv file.csv'. Filter rows: '$data | Where-Object {$_.Column -eq "value"}'. Export results: 'Export-Csv output.csv -NoTypeInformation'. PowerShell automatically maps CSV headers to object properties, making it easy to process tabular data without needing a separate scripting environment.

question: What is Windows PE (Preinstallation Environment) versus Windows RE (Recovery Environment)?
answer: Windows PE is a lightweight Windows for deployment and recovery tasks, used by IT professionals for imaging and troubleshooting. Windows RE (Recovery Environment) is built into Windows and accessed via the boot menu, offering Startup Repair, System Restore, Command Prompt, and System Image Recovery for end-user recovery scenarios.

question: How do I enable font smoothing in Windows?
answer: Right-click the desktop, select 'Personalize > Colors', then search for 'Adjust the appearance and performance of Windows'. In the Performance Options dialog, check 'Smooth edges of screen fonts' under Visual Effects. You can also use the ClearType Text Tuner (search in Start) to fine-tune how text is rendered on your display.

question: How do I use 'watch' command in Linux?
answer: The 'watch' command repeatedly runs another command and displays its output, refreshing at a set interval. 'watch -n 5 df -h' shows disk space usage every 5 seconds. 'watch -d command' highlights differences between runs. Press Ctrl+C to stop. It's very useful for monitoring log files, disk usage, or network stats in real time.

question: How do I configure Windows to use a proxy server?
answer: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy. Under 'Manual proxy setup', enable 'Use a proxy server' and enter the server address and port. You can also enter addresses that should bypass the proxy. Alternatively, configure the proxy in your browser's network settings for browser-only proxying.

question: How do I install and configure Nginx on Linux?
answer: Install with 'sudo apt install nginx'. Start and enable with 'sudo systemctl start nginx && sudo systemctl enable nginx'. Configuration files are in /etc/nginx/. The default site config is /etc/nginx/sites-available/default. After editing, test config with 'sudo nginx -t' and reload with 'sudo systemctl reload nginx'.

question: What is a kernel module in Linux and how do I load one?
answer: Kernel modules are pieces of code that can be loaded into the kernel on demand to extend functionality (e.g., drivers). 'lsmod' lists loaded modules. 'sudo modprobe modulename' loads a module. 'sudo modprobe -r modulename' unloads it. 'sudo insmod /path/to/module.ko' loads a module from a specific file.

question: How do I convert between file formats using FFmpeg on Linux?
answer: FFmpeg is a powerful multimedia converter. 'ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi' converts formats. 'ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vn output.mp3' extracts audio. 'ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vf scale=1280:720 output.mp4' resizes video. Install with 'sudo apt install ffmpeg'. FFmpeg supports virtually every audio and video format.

question: What is the purpose of /proc filesystem in Linux?
answer: The /proc virtual filesystem provides a window into the kernel and running processes. /proc/cpuinfo shows CPU details, /proc/meminfo shows memory stats, and /proc/[PID]/ contains information about each running process. These aren't real files — they're kernel data structures presented as a filesystem for easy reading.

question: How do I set up passwordless SSH between two Linux machines?
answer: Generate an SSH key pair on the source machine with 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519'. Copy the public key to the destination with 'ssh-copy-id user@destination'. Now 'ssh user@destination' connects without a password. The private key on your machine acts as the credential. Protect it with a passphrase for added security.

question: How do I create a custom keyboard shortcut in Windows?
answer: Right-click the shortcut for the application and select Properties. In the 'Shortcut key' field, click and press your desired key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Alt+C). Click OK. Windows will now launch the application when you press that key combination, as long as the shortcut is in the Start menu or desktop.

question: How do I use 'journalctl' to filter logs in Linux?
answer: journalctl -u servicename' shows logs for a specific service. 'journalctl --since "2024-01-01" --until "2024-01-31"' filters by date range. 'journalctl -p err' shows only error-level messages. 'journalctl -f' follows new log entries in real time. 'journalctl --disk-usage' shows how much space logs are consuming.

question: How do I reset network settings in macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Network. Select the network interface (Wi-Fi or Ethernet), click the minus button to delete it, then click the plus button to re-add it. You can also delete all network locations and create a new 'Automatic' location. For persistent issues, delete files in /Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/.

question: What is Automator Quick Action on macOS and how do I use it?
answer: A Quick Action is a type of Automator workflow that appears in the right-click context menu in Finder or in the Touch Bar. Create one in Automator by selecting 'Quick Action' as the workflow type. Set 'Workflow receives' to files or folders, add your actions, and save. The Quick Action then appears when you right-click files in Finder.

question: How do I use the 'alias' command in Linux/macOS?
answer: The alias command creates shortcuts for longer commands. 'alias ll="ls -la"' makes 'll' run 'ls -la'. Add aliases to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc to make them permanent. 'alias' with no arguments lists current aliases. 'unalias name' removes an alias. Aliases only exist in the current shell unless saved to a profile file.

question: How do I check system boot time in Linux?
answer: Run 'uptime' or 'uptime -p' for a human-readable uptime. 'who -b' shows the last boot time. 'systemd-analyze' shows total boot time and 'systemd-analyze blame' lists services by how long they took to start, helping identify slow boot causes.

question: How do I fix a corrupt user profile in Windows?
answer: Create a new local user account. Log into the new account, then copy files from C:\Users\OldUsername to the new profile folder. Use regedit to merge registry settings if needed. Microsoft's User Profile Service troubleshooter can sometimes automatically repair a corrupt profile. Check the Event Viewer for specific errors related to the profile service.

question: What is the Windows Registry and what does it store?
answer: The Windows Registry is a hierarchical database storing configuration settings for the OS, hardware, and installed applications. It contains keys and values for user preferences, system policies, driver information, and application settings. Editing it incorrectly can break Windows, so always export a backup before making changes.

question: How do I repair corrupted system files in Windows?
answer: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run 'sfc /scannow'. This System File Checker scans all protected system files and replaces corrupted ones. If SFC finds issues it can't fix, run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' first, then run sfc again. A restart may be required.

question: What is the difference between Sleep and Hibernate in Windows?
answer: Sleep saves your open work to RAM and uses a small amount of power, allowing fast wake-up. Hibernate saves everything to the hard drive and uses no power, but takes longer to resume. Hibernate is better for extended periods away from power; Sleep is better for short breaks.

question: How do I pin an app to the Windows taskbar?
answer: Right-click the app in the Start menu or when it's running in the taskbar, then select 'Pin to taskbar'. You can also drag app shortcuts to the taskbar. To rearrange pinned apps, simply drag them left or right along the taskbar.

question: How do I use Windows Sandbox?
answer: Windows Sandbox is available on Windows 10/11 Pro and Enterprise. Enable it via 'Turn Windows features on or off', check 'Windows Sandbox', and restart. Launch it from the Start menu to get a clean, isolated Windows environment that resets completely every time you close it — ideal for testing suspicious software.

question: How do I find large files wasting space in Windows?
answer: Open File Explorer, click in the search bar, and use the filter 'Size: Gigantic (>128MB)'. Alternatively, use free tools like WinDirStat or TreeSize Free which visualize your disk usage as a graphical tree map, making it easy to spot the largest files and folders.

question: What is PowerShell and how is it different from Command Prompt?
answer: PowerShell is a more powerful shell and scripting language built on .NET, designed for system administration. Command Prompt (cmd) is the older, simpler command-line interface. PowerShell can manipulate objects and data structures, access Windows APIs, and automate complex tasks that are impossible or cumbersome in cmd.

question: How do I enable Hyper-V on Windows?
answer: Go to 'Turn Windows features on or off' in Control Panel, check 'Hyper-V', and click OK. Restart your PC. Hyper-V requires Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise, or Education, and a 64-bit CPU with virtualization support enabled in BIOS. Launch 'Hyper-V Manager' from the Start menu to create and manage virtual machines.

question: How do I schedule automatic shutdowns in Windows?
answer: Open Task Scheduler, click 'Create Basic Task', name it, set the trigger (daily, weekly, etc.), choose 'Start a program' as the action, and enter 'shutdown.exe' with arguments '/s /f /t 0'. For a one-time shutdown, you can also run 'shutdown /s /t 3600' in Command Prompt to shut down in 1 hour.

question: How do I use Windows 11's virtual desktops feature?
answer: Press Windows + Tab to open Task View. Click 'New desktop' to create a virtual desktop. You can drag app windows between desktops or right-click a window to move it. Use Windows + Ctrl + Arrow keys to switch between desktops quickly. Virtual desktops are great for separating work and personal contexts.

question: What is the difference between FAT32, NTFS, and exFAT file systems?
answer: FAT32 is widely compatible with all devices but has a 4GB single file size limit. NTFS is the Windows standard, supporting large files, permissions, encryption, and journaling, but has limited compatibility with non-Windows systems. exFAT is designed for flash drives — compatible with both Windows and Mac, no 4GB file size limit.

question: How do I enable BitLocker drive encryption on Windows?
answer: Open Control Panel > System and Security > BitLocker Drive Encryption. Click 'Turn on BitLocker' next to your drive. You can unlock with a password or TPM chip. Save your recovery key to Microsoft account, USB, or print it. BitLocker requires Windows 10/11 Pro or Enterprise.

question: How do I install a .deb package in Ubuntu Linux?
answer: Use the command 'sudo dpkg -i package.deb'. If there are missing dependencies, run 'sudo apt-get install -f' afterward to resolve them. Alternatively, use 'sudo apt install ./package.deb' which handles dependencies automatically. You can also double-click the .deb file in the Files app to open it in the Software Center.

question: How do I enable SSH on Ubuntu?
answer: Install the OpenSSH server with 'sudo apt install openssh-server'. Start and enable the service with 'sudo systemctl enable --now ssh'. Check the status with 'sudo systemctl status ssh'. The firewall rule can be added with 'sudo ufw allow ssh'. Connect from another machine using 'ssh username@ip-address'.

question: What is a Linux shell script and how do I run one?
answer: A shell script is a text file containing a series of Linux commands that execute sequentially. Create one with a text editor, start with '#!/bin/bash' on the first line, add your commands, save as 'script.sh'. Make it executable with 'chmod +x script.sh' and run it with './script.sh' from the same directory.

question: How do I manage services in Linux with systemctl?
answer: Use 'sudo systemctl start servicename' to start a service, 'sudo systemctl stop servicename' to stop it, and 'sudo systemctl enable servicename' to make it start automatically at boot. 'sudo systemctl status servicename' shows whether it's running and recent log entries. 'sudo systemctl restart' restarts a running service.

question: How do I set up automatic updates on Ubuntu?
answer: Install the unattended-upgrades package: 'sudo apt install unattended-upgrades'. Enable it with 'sudo dpkg-reconfigure --priority=low unattended-upgrades'. Configuration is in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50unattended-upgrades where you can specify which packages to auto-update, typically security updates only.

question: What is a package manager in Linux and how does it work?
answer: A package manager automates installing, updating, and removing software by fetching packages from repositories and handling all dependencies. Ubuntu/Debian use 'apt', Red Hat/Fedora use 'dnf' or 'yum', and Arch uses 'pacman'. The package manager knows which libraries each program needs and installs them automatically.

question: How do I mount and unmount drives in Linux?
answer: Use 'sudo mount /dev/sdX1 /mnt/foldername' to mount a partition. Create the mount point folder first with 'mkdir'. To unmount, use 'sudo umount /mnt/foldername'. To auto-mount at boot, add an entry to /etc/fstab. Use 'lsblk' or 'fdisk -l' to identify your disk device names.

question: How do I view and kill processes in Linux?
answer: Use 'ps aux' to list all processes with their PIDs. Use 'top' or 'htop' for real-time monitoring. Kill a process by PID with 'kill PID' or 'kill -9 PID' for a force kill. Use 'killall processname' to kill all instances by name. 'pkill processname' also works and supports pattern matching.

question: What is the difference between sudo and su in Linux?
answer: 'sudo' runs a single command with elevated (root) privileges without switching user. 'su' switches your current session to the root user entirely, requiring the root password. 'sudo -i' or 'sudo su' opens a root shell. For security, 'sudo' is preferred because it logs commands and doesn't require sharing the root password.

question: How do I configure a static IP address in Ubuntu?
answer: Edit the Netplan configuration file in /etc/netplan/ (e.g., 00-installer-config.yaml). Set 'dhcp4: no' and specify 'addresses', 'gateway4', and 'nameservers'. Apply changes with 'sudo netplan apply'. Verify the new IP with 'ip addr show'. Netplan replaced ifupdown in Ubuntu 18.04 and later.

question: How do I check system uptime in Linux?
answer: Run the 'uptime' command in terminal — it shows how long the system has been running, the number of users, and load averages for the past 1, 5, and 15 minutes. 'who -b' shows the last boot time. 'journalctl --list-boots' shows a history of all boot events.

question: How do I configure automatic login on macOS?
answer: Go to System Preferences > Users & Groups > Login Options. Click the lock to authenticate, then set 'Automatic login' to your user account. Note that enabling automatic login disables FileVault encryption, so it's only recommended for low-risk single-user machines not storing sensitive data.

question: What is Spotlight on macOS and how do I use it?
answer: Spotlight is macOS's built-in search and quick-launch tool. Press Command + Space to open it and type anything — app names, files, contacts, calculations, unit conversions, or questions answered by Siri Suggestions. It can also search within files for their content, making it a powerful productivity tool.

question: How do I reset PRAM/NVRAM on a Mac?
answer: Shut down your Mac. Press the power button, then immediately hold Command + Option + P + R. Keep holding for about 20 seconds — the Mac will appear to restart. Release the keys. On Apple Silicon Macs, NVRAM resets automatically during the startup process, so a manual reset isn't needed.

question: How do I use the macOS Activity Monitor?
answer: Open Activity Monitor from Applications > Utilities or search with Spotlight. It shows all running processes with their CPU, memory, energy, disk, and network usage. Click on any column header to sort. Quit unresponsive processes by selecting them and clicking the X button at the top. It's equivalent to Windows Task Manager.

question: How do I enable or disable System Integrity Protection (SIP) on Mac?
answer: SIP protects system files from modification even by root users. To disable it, restart in Recovery Mode (hold Command+R on Intel, hold power on Apple Silicon), open Terminal, and run 'csrutil disable'. To re-enable, run 'csrutil enable'. Only disable SIP if you have a specific need, as it's an important security layer.

question: How do I use macOS's built-in screen reader, VoiceOver?
answer: Enable VoiceOver with Command + F5 or via System Preferences > Accessibility > VoiceOver. It reads aloud screen content, interactive elements, and notifications. Use the VoiceOver keys (Control + Option) combined with arrows to navigate. VoiceOver supports Braille displays and is fully integrated with all native macOS apps.

question: How do I set up a Python virtual environment?
answer: Run 'python3 -m venv myenv' to create the virtual environment in a folder called 'myenv'. Activate it with 'source myenv/bin/activate' on Mac/Linux or 'myenv\Scripts\activate' on Windows. Install packages with pip inside the activated environment. Deactivate with 'deactivate'. This isolates project dependencies from the system Python.

question: How do I update Python packages with pip?
answer: Run 'pip install --upgrade packagename' to update a specific package. To update all packages, use 'pip list --outdated' to see what needs updating, then update each one. The command 'pip install --upgrade pip' updates pip itself. In a virtual environment, changes only affect that environment.

question: What is Docker and how does it differ from a virtual machine?
answer: Docker uses containerization — containers share the host OS kernel but are isolated from each other, making them lightweight and fast to start. Virtual machines run a full OS on virtualized hardware, using more resources. Docker containers package an application with its dependencies, ensuring it runs the same on any host machine with Docker installed.

question: How do I check open ports on my system?
answer: On Windows, run 'netstat -ano' in Command Prompt to see listening ports and the associated process IDs. On Linux/macOS, use 'ss -tlnp' or 'netstat -tlnp'. The command 'sudo lsof -i :portnum' shows which process is using a specific port. These commands help identify unexpected network listeners.

question: How do I set up Git for the first time?
answer: Install Git from git-scm.com. Configure your identity: 'git config --global user.name "Your Name"' and 'git config --global user.email "you@example.com"'. Set your default editor and branch name. Generate an SSH key for GitHub/GitLab authentication using 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519'.

question: How do I dual-boot Windows and macOS (Hackintosh)?
answer: Running macOS on non-Apple hardware is complex, unsupported, and violates Apple's EULA. You'll need a compatible CPU/GPU, a bootloader like OpenCore, and macOS installation files. The process requires extensive configuration and often breaks after OS updates. A virtual machine or purchasing a Mac is strongly recommended instead.

question: How do I run Windows programs on Linux using Wine?
answer: Install Wine via your package manager (e.g., 'sudo apt install wine'). Run a Windows executable with 'wine program.exe'. For better compatibility, use PlayOnLinux or Bottles as graphical frontends. Lutris is excellent for Windows games. Not all programs work under Wine — check the Wine AppDB for compatibility ratings.

question: How do I use the Task Scheduler in Windows?
answer: Open Task Scheduler from the Start menu. Click 'Create Basic Task' for a simple wizard or 'Create Task' for advanced options. Set a trigger (time, system event, logon), an action (run a program, send email, show message), and conditions/settings. Scheduled tasks run even if you're not logged in (if configured with highest privileges).

question: What is Bash and how is it different from sh?
answer: Bash (Bourne Again Shell) is the most common default shell on Linux systems, offering features like command history, tab completion, arrays, and more complex scripting constructs. sh (POSIX shell) is simpler and more portable but lacks many Bash conveniences. Scripts using Bash-specific features should use '#!/bin/bash' rather than '#!/bin/sh'.

question: How do I access Windows from Linux using Remote Desktop?
answer: Install 'rdesktop' or 'Remmina' on Linux. Ensure Remote Desktop is enabled on the Windows machine. Launch Remmina, create a new connection, select RDP protocol, and enter the Windows machine's IP address and credentials. FreeRDP is another popular alternative with good compatibility.

question: How do I enable Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2)?
answer: Run 'wsl --install' in an elevated PowerShell — this installs WSL2 and Ubuntu by default. If WSL1 is already installed, update to WSL2 with 'wsl --set-default-version 2'. Set a specific distro to WSL2 with 'wsl --set-version Ubuntu 2'. WSL2 uses a real Linux kernel and offers better file system performance than WSL1.

question: How do I change the hostname on Linux?
answer: Run 'sudo hostnamectl set-hostname newhostname' to change the hostname immediately. Edit /etc/hosts to update any references to the old hostname there. The change persists across reboots. Verify the change with 'hostnamectl' or 'hostname'. On older systems, you may need to edit /etc/hostname directly.

question: How do I check memory usage in macOS?
answer: Open Activity Monitor and click the 'Memory' tab. It shows memory pressure (green/yellow/red indicator), used and cached memory, and which apps use the most RAM. 'Memory pressure' is a better indicator than raw usage — green means plenty available; red means the system is actively swapping to disk.

question: What is GRUB and how do I update it in Linux?
answer: GRUB (Grand Unified Bootloader) is the bootloader used by most Linux distributions to manage the boot process. After installing a new kernel or changing settings, run 'sudo update-grub' (Debian/Ubuntu) or 'sudo grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg' (Red Hat/Fedora). GRUB config files are stored in /etc/default/grub.

question: How do I create and use aliases in Linux?
answer: Add an alias to your ~/.bashrc file: 'alias ll="ls -la"'. Run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply immediately. Aliases persist across terminal sessions once in the profile file. List all current aliases with 'alias' (no arguments). Remove a temporary alias with 'unalias aliasname'.

question: How do I use macOS's built-in disk utility to repair drives?
answer: Open Disk Utility from Applications > Utilities. Select the disk or volume in the left panel and click 'First Aid', then 'Run'. This checks and repairs filesystem errors. For the startup disk, boot into Recovery Mode (Command+R) and run First Aid from there, since the active startup disk can't fully repair itself while in use.

question: How do I set the PATH variable in Linux?
answer: Add 'export PATH=$PATH:/new/directory' to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile file. Run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply changes. The PATH variable tells the shell where to look for executable programs. Use 'echo $PATH' to see the current value. System-wide PATH changes go in /etc/environment or /etc/profile.

question: What is the difference between a soft link and a hard link in Linux?
answer: A soft (symbolic) link is a pointer to another file's path — it breaks if the original file is deleted or moved. A hard link is another directory entry pointing to the same inode (actual data) as the original — deleting the original doesn't affect the hard link. Create them with 'ln -s target linkname' (soft) or 'ln target linkname' (hard).

question: How do I configure Windows to require a password after sleep?
answer: Go to Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options. Under 'Require sign-in', select 'When PC wakes up from sleep'. This adds security when you step away. You can also set a shorter screen saver timeout with a password prompt via Screen saver settings in the Control Panel.

question: How do I use Windows Defender Offline Scan?
answer: Go to Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options, select 'Windows Defender Offline scan', and click 'Scan now'. This restarts your PC and runs a deep scan before Windows boots, catching malware that hides from normal scans. It takes about 15 minutes and the PC restarts automatically when done.

question: How do I check if a port is open using PowerShell?
answer: Use 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName hostname -Port 443' in PowerShell to check if a port is reachable. It shows TcpTestSucceeded: True if the port is open and accessible. You can also use 'telnet hostname port' if Telnet is enabled, or the classic 'netstat -an' to list all open local ports.

question: How do I enable automatic login to a domain account in Windows?
answer: Open the Run dialog (Win+R), type 'netplwiz', and uncheck 'Users must enter a user name and password'. Enter your domain credentials in the dialog that appears. Note that this stores credentials and reduces security — only use on physically secured machines. Group Policy may prevent this on managed domain computers.

question: What is the Windows Page File and how should I configure it?
answer: The Page File is virtual memory on the hard drive used when RAM is full. Windows manages it automatically by default, which works well for most users. Manual configuration is in System Properties > Advanced > Performance > Virtual Memory. Setting a fixed size (e.g., 1.5x RAM) can slightly improve performance on high-load servers.

question: How do I stop Windows Update from restarting my PC automatically?
answer: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > Advanced Options. Enable 'Notify to schedule restart' and set Active Hours so Windows won't restart during your work hours. Windows Pro and Enterprise users can pause updates for up to 35 days or use Group Policy for more granular control.

question: How do I change the Windows login screen background?
answer: Go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen. Under 'Background', choose Picture or Slideshow for a custom image, or Windows Spotlight for rotating Bing images. To change the sign-in background specifically, enable 'Show lock screen background picture on the sign-in screen'.

question: How do I defragment my hard drive in Windows?
answer: Search for 'Defragment and Optimize Drives' in the Start menu and open it. Select your HDD and click 'Optimize'. Note: do NOT defragment SSDs — Windows shows 'Trim' instead, which is the correct optimization for SSDs. HDDs benefit from defragmentation; SSDs do not.

question: How do I use Robocopy to mirror folders in Windows?
answer: Robocopy is a powerful command-line copy tool. Use 'robocopy Source Destination /MIR' to mirror a directory (copies new/changed files and deletes removed ones). Add '/Z' for restartable copies and '/LOG:file.txt' to log output. Robocopy is much more reliable than xcopy for large or network transfers.

question: How do I run a program as a different user in Windows?
answer: Hold Shift and right-click the program icon, then select 'Run as different user'. Enter the username and password for the account you want to use. This is useful for running admin tools while logged in as a standard user without fully switching accounts.

question: How do I enable verbose startup and shutdown messages in Windows?
answer: Open Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc), go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System, and enable 'Display highly detailed status messages'. This shows exactly what Windows is doing during startup and shutdown, useful for diagnosing slow boot issues.

question: What is the Windows Event Viewer and how do I use it?
answer: Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) logs all system, security, and application events. Expand Windows Logs and check 'System' for hardware and OS errors, 'Application' for app crashes, and 'Security' for login events. Filter logs by Event Level (Error, Warning) and look for patterns around the time an issue occurred.

question: How do I list all installed software from the Command Prompt?
answer: Run 'wmic product get name,version' in Command Prompt for a list of installed MSI packages. In PowerShell, 'Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion' gives a more complete list. Export results to a file with '> software.txt'.

question: How do I use the Windows Resource Monitor?
answer: Open Task Manager and click 'Open Resource Monitor' at the bottom, or search for 'resmon'. It provides detailed tabs for CPU, Memory, Disk, and Network showing exactly which processes are using each resource and how much. It's more granular than Task Manager and useful for finding bottlenecks.

question: How do I lock down a Windows PC for public use (Kiosk Mode)?
answer: Windows 10/11 has a built-in Assigned Access feature. Go to Settings > Accounts > Family & other users > Set up a kiosk. Create or select a local account, choose which app runs in full screen. The kiosk user can only use that one app. For more advanced lockdowns, use Windows Configuration Designer or Group Policy.

question: How do I check my Linux kernel version?
answer: Run 'uname -r' to display the current kernel version. 'uname -a' shows full system information including kernel, hostname, and architecture. 'cat /proc/version' gives even more detail including the GCC version used to compile the kernel. 'hostnamectl' on systemd systems also shows the kernel version.

question: How do I add a user to the sudoers file in Linux?
answer: The safest method is to add the user to the sudo group: 'sudo usermod -aG sudo username' (Debian/Ubuntu) or 'sudo usermod -aG wheel username' (Red Hat/Fedora). To give fine-grained control, edit the sudoers file with 'sudo visudo' and add a line like 'username ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' for passwordless sudo.

question: What is LVM (Logical Volume Manager) in Linux?
answer: LVM provides flexible disk management by abstracting physical storage into logical volumes. You can resize volumes on the fly, span volumes across multiple disks, and create snapshots. Key commands: 'pvcreate' (physical volume), 'vgcreate' (volume group), 'lvcreate' (logical volume). LVM is commonly used on servers for easy storage management.

question: What is the /etc/hosts file in Linux and what is it used for?
answer: The /etc/hosts file maps hostnames to IP addresses locally, bypassing DNS. It's read before DNS, so entries here override DNS resolution.
